name: DesertRevenge
source:
I looked out across the vast desert. I have been chasing the creature for the past year. I finally would have him. Word has spread that Mr. Stevens is staying in the town not far ahead, or at least he's been moving towards it. I rode in. 
 
 The town was called Cliff's edge. It was an old mining town back in the early 1800's before most settlers headed west. It was rich until the mine dried up. Now it seems its just people who do n't have anywhere else to go. I guess after I confront Mr. Stevens I wo n't have anywhere to go, so Ill fit right in. The town made me think of back home. I lived just outside of Chicago with a wife and young daughter. Mr. Stevens was a big time gangster from New York. I was a copper, irish born and raised until I moved out here. I had infiltrated his gang and after discovering me, he killed my wife and daughter. I swore I would n't let him live. I skipped town after hearing that Stevens had headed west. 
 
 Every small town he visits, every inn he's stayed at. I've tracked him to. And each time, I hear stories about how he killed someone in the town. He knew I was following him and he was getting anxious. I had telagramed the chief back in Chicago. He was an old friend of mine, so he said he'd send someone out to help catch Stevens. I told him where Stevens was headed and he said he'd have a man waiting. Good ol' chief, always had my back. I stopped into the bar. 
 
 `` So,'' I said `` Anyone new come to town lately.'' 
 
 The barkeep looked nervous at me. She came closer and whispered `` Listen, we do n't want any trouble.'' 
 
 He was here. His influence had already crept into the hearts of the locals. I walked over to the inn. I got a room and as the inn keeper had her back turned I looked at the ledger. 
 
 *Stevens room 5* 
 
 I took my key to room 2 but headed to 5. I walked up the stairs. He was here, and if he was n't Id wait. Id wait for him until I could catch him. As I walked towards the room, I looked down towards the inn keep. She was talking to a man I had n't noticed before. He glanced up at me. I walked faster towards room 5. It was hidden from the view of the lobby. Perfect. 
 
 I imagined my daughter, my wife, and all the people who died. All screaming for me to open the door and kill this man. I drew my revolver. I lightly touched the door knob. It was open. I burst in. Saw him at the mirror. Before he turned around I fired my pistol. He was dead before he hit the floor. 
 
 I could almost see the gangsters face as I walked towards the body. I had seen it once when I was working in Chicago. I knelt down and turned over the body. I felt sick. This was not Stevens. The man from the lobby walked in, rifle raised. 
 
 `` Ok calm down.'' He said `` My name is Aurthurs, from the CPD.'' I raised my pistol, but dropped it almost immediately. `` Ive been sent here by the chief to help you. We can fix this. You can still catch the real Stevens. He's on his way towards Montgomery Utah. If you leave now, Ill send a man out there. We can just say that Stevens did this.'' 
 
 I nodded. I could n't have killed a civilian. I had to go. I ran outside. Seeing my horse I left Cliff's edge. I would find another town to rest up in and then head towards Montgomery. 
 
 **Aurthurs report # 12** 
 Chief STOP Made contact with project Stevens STOP Send next gangster to Montgomery Utah STOP 
 **End Aurthurs report # 12** 
 
 I looked out across the vast desert...
retelling:
**Narrative Perspective: The Barkeep at Cliff's Edge**

   In a remote corner of the American West, nestled between the jagged cliffs and the vast desert expanse, lies an old, forlorn mining town called Cliff's Edge. It is home to the weary and the unwanted, survivors of another era who eke out a living on the precipice of oblivion. Among them is a nervous woman working at the local bar, known only as the Barkeep.

   One fateful day, a stranger wandered into the bar, his eyes burning with an intensity that chilled the heart. The Barkeep had seen many travelers pass through, but there was something different about this man - a hardness etched into his very being, a hunger for vengeance that hung heavy in the air like the dust from the desert floor. He called himself the Narrator, and he spoke of a New York gangster named Mr. Stevens who had taken everything from him - his wife, his daughter, his peace.

   The Barkeep listened, her heart pounding in her chest as she imagined the terrible tragedy that must have befallen this man. She couldn't help but feel a pang of sympathy for him, even as he ordered another round and cast suspicious glances around the room. As the evening wore on, the Narrator grew more agitated, his questions about Mr. Stevens becoming increasingly insistent.

   The next morning, the Barkeep watched as the Narrator stormed out of the bar, headed for the inn where she knew he believed Mr. Stevens to be hiding. She could only hope that he would find what he sought and leave their forsaken town behind, taking his torment with him.

   Days passed, and the Narrator returned, his face twisted in a mask of rage. He burst into the inn, shots ringing through the air like the echoes of long-forgotten hopes. The Barkeep heard screams, followed by silence, and she knew that something terrible had occurred.

   As the dust settled, another man emerged from the inn - an officer from Chicago named Aurthurs. He spoke with the Narrator, their voices low and urgent, but the Barkeep couldn't make out what they said. Then, as suddenly as it had begun, the confrontation was over, and the Narrator left Cliff's Edge once more, heading east towards Montgomery, Utah.

   As she went about her work that day, the Barkeep couldn't help but wonder about the fate of the innocent man who had been gunned down in his sleep. She hoped that the Narrator would find what he sought and finally find peace, but she knew that such a thing was unlikely for someone like him. In this godforsaken town, where even hope was scarce, it seemed as though vengeance was all that remained.

name: GodsBetrayalAndRedemption
source:
`` Oh me dammit he's actually doing it!'' The Father said as the masses were beginning to follow Jesus' beliefs. God wondered how to end his son's little adventure, but in a way that would n't make him a martyr. He came upon the idea that one of his disciples would betray him for a measly sum of 20 silver and that the Roman's would be the one's to do it. This would show the people that humanity can not be saved. Oh and they would hate those damn Pagan Romans 
 
 `` Jesus you are ending your little game and you are coming back home. I'll have somebody betray you to show you humanity is devious.'' 
 
 `` Who would do something like that? My apostles love me.'' 
 
 `` I do n't know, Peter or Judas I have n't decided yet. Probably both. Oh and this betrayal is going to involve torture, because you are still grounded for trying to defy my order to forsake humanity.'' 
 
 Jesus got his disciples together for his last supper. Here he did some handy investigation work with some dipped bread that resulted in Judas being pinned as the turncloak. This was a bummer because Jesus loved Judas ( although he loved everyone else just as much ). After his investigation Jesus went to pray. 
 
 `` Dad please do n't do this, I'm making a lot of progress! We could finally remove the original sin from the Earth and return paradise to humanity.'' 
 
 `` Say it again I dare you! Humanity can not be saved. I will prove this to you by showing you, firsthand, the brutality of human action.'' God then went to oversee other business as Jesus was seized by the Judas led Romans. 
 
 God made Jesus' punishment as harsh as possible, not only to show his son that humans were still capable of evil acts, but also to show anyone looking back that Jesus had failed. God was then shocked as the human's defied his will multiple times to try and save Jesus. First the Romans of all people find Jesus innocent. Then Peter, who was ordered by God to deny Christ, repents and accepts him as his lord. Following this Judas, the original turncloak, also repents, abandoning his silver reward. God rectifies the Roman verdict by compelling the people to free a different man instead, and it all ends up working out in the end as Jesus gives an ambiguous answer to the Roman question `` Are you King of the Jews?''. `` Say all you want about those Roman, but they hate dissenters just as much as me.'' God said to some angels with a bit of glib in his holy voice. 
 
 God then guides the torture to be a mockery of his son's `` royalty'', but even more signs of humanities faith in Jesus come as still people in the crowd defy God's wishes and love Christ. 
 
 `` Father, Father, why have you forsaken me!?'' These words shake the Father. God realizes that it was n't Humanity that ordained this torture upon his son, it was God himself. God felt terrible, he had just subjected his son to torture because he was too stubborn to see that Jesus was n't just rebelling against his father, but was showing his father a crude truth. A final act of human defiance, a Roman soldier thrusting his spear into Jesus' side as a sign of mercy, made God finally come to the conclusion that Jesus had tried so hard to show him. 
 
 Humanity can be saved.
retelling:
From the perspective of Peter, the fisherman turned apostle:

In the land of Judea, amidst a sea of souls yearning for salvation, I walked side by side with my master, Jesus, the son of God. His teachings resonated within me like the gentle lapping of waves against the shore, filling my heart with an unwavering faith that I had never known before.

One fateful night, as we gathered to break bread and share stories at the Last Supper, a palpable tension filled the air. Unbeknownst to us, the hour of betrayal was upon us. Judas, my brother in Christ, knelt beside me, his eyes devoid of the warmth that once shone there. Little did I know that he would soon betray our Lord for thirty pieces of silver.

As we made our way from the supper, our path illuminated by moonlight, I felt a gnawing fear take root in my heart. In the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus prayed fervently, his anguish heavy upon me like a suffocating cloak. The weight of his impending suffering threatened to crush me, yet I could do nothing but stand by and watch as God's plan unfolded before my eyes.

In the morning, Roman soldiers surrounded us, their steel swords glinting menacingly in the early light. Jesus, ever calm and composed, faced them bravely, his love for humanity shining brightly even in the face of imminent death. I, filled with cowardice, denied knowing him three times, my heart heavy with shame.

As we were led to the site of crucifixion, I could feel the malevolence radiating from the masses that had gathered to witness Jesus' torture and execution. The Roman officials, however, found Jesus innocent, a testament to his righteousness. Yet, God, my Creator, manipulated events to ensure Jesus' suffering would continue.

Judas, consumed by guilt, sought redemption but was denied. In the end, it was not the brutality of Jesus' crucifixion that shattered my faith in humanity's inherent depravity, but the countless acts of defiance from the crowd and even a Roman soldier's act of mercy that ultimately led God to realize his error.

In that moment, I felt an overwhelming sense of gratitude for Jesus' unwavering love and sacrifice. The realization that humanity was capable of salvation filled me with newfound hope, and I vowed to spread the teachings of Jesus, the son of God, for all time.

name: HarlemHold
source:
`` Lieutenant, form up for men at the church on Malcolm X and one hundred and eleventh, I want a goddamned defensive line now!'' 
 
 Major Bellamy roars the words, I obey. That's my job. 
 
 I have sixteen men. 
 
 Men. More like boys. Sergeant Colville is the only one who's seen any real service or spent any time in the shit. The rest of my NCOs have n't even bothered to show up, leaving me at half strength and without a real command structure. 
 
 The only saving grace in this whole mess is that we managed to scavenge the armory first. 
 
 I lead my men to the area the Major is referring to, a small church front on the southeast corner. The Major's plan is ambitious for how many guardsmen we have, as well as whatever NYPD officers managed to get here. 
 
 He's building a perimeter around Central Park. 
 
 He's using Columbus and Park, we'll use the Kennedy reservoir as a natural buffer so we can save defending that area. My men are the farthest north point at 111th. 
 
 It's ambitious. 
 
 To say the least. 
 
 Command structure is shot to shit, the rioting in Washington took out the JCs from what I hear. Not to mention our own goddamned Colonel is missing. 
 
 I set two guys to moving cars and a transport truck across as our first line of defense, until the engineers get around to some proper entrenching this is what we've got. 
 
 I hear footsteps from behind, turning and readying my weapon. 
 
 NYPD officers, two SWAT and a couple of beat cops. 
 
 Reinforcements. 
 
 What a joke. 
 
 `` Orders sir?'' the first, a Sergeant, asks me. 
 
 `` I want your SWAT guys on the flanks of my men, rest of you can take the center. Cascading defenses.'' 
 
 They understand, loping off to comply. 
 
 What a shit storm. 
 
 Economy collapses and people turn into savages. Riots, murder, looting. Rape. 
 
 God, the screams. 
 
 I've blocked them out as much as I can but it's still near and far too vivid. 
 
 Smoke from too many fires chokes the sky, New York is burning. 
 
 Food and water will go first. 
 
 If the ammo does n't. 
 
 I have twenty three men, fresh faced kids. 
 
 Just down that street are thousands of angry people that want our guns. Our rations. And thousands more that need our protection. 
 
 God. 
 
 What a mess. 
 
 ***** 
 
 Our defensive line is weak at best. 
 
 One of the guys was a truck driver, claimed he could tip the damn thing on it's side. 
 
 I do n't know how, I really do n't, but he managed it. 
 
 The thing is laying sideways across the road behind a first line of cars. Six men, and the SWAT officers, on top of the overturned trailer. 
 
 Four of my guys are now engineers, finding anything they can use to make cover. It's New York, there are going to be some guns out there. 
 
 It's haphazard and it's rough but it will have to do. 
 
 There's a fairly steady stream of civilians running our way. Two of the beat cops are lost to taking them to the park, where there's the semblance of a safe zone. 
 
 Most concerning is the news that one of these folks pass along as they make their way past. 
 
 `` Big crowd back there, bunch of thugs burning and stealing and spoiling for a fight. At least two hundred.'' 
 
 Well shit. 
 
 I check my watch for the hundredth time, 4:07 PM flashing at me. 
 
 `` Sir!'' one of my guys, Pearson, shouts from on top of the trailer. He's the best shot we have. Which is n't saying much. `` A truck is coming around the corner up there!'' 
 
 Gunfire starts up the street, chasing the pick up truck. Big vehicle for a tight city. 
 
 `` Positions!'' 
 
 It's my voice, louder than I expected. Thank god for training. 
 
 The boys move into a firing line, readying their weapons. Most of them are shaking, terrified. 
 
 I am too. I just hide it better. 
 
 The truck careens towards us, before another appears behind it. Then a transport truck. Then a car. They're roaring their way towards us, engines revving. 
 
 `` Hold fire!'' 
 
 My voice again. I react faster than my mind processes. That's a good sign. 
 
 There's a NYPD cop hanging off the side of the transport, waving at us. He looks rough. 
 
 The convoy pulls to a stop, the cop dismounts and sprints towards us, breathing heavily and dripping sweat. Thankfully the gunfire stops when they get close to us. Apparently the sight of sixteen National Guardsmen is enough of a deterrent. 
 
 `` Sir, we've got... supplies.'' 
 
 He grins. 
 
 I like him. 
 
 I have my guys back up the cars, opening a space for the vehicles. 
 
 I send my guys back to the line and meet the newcomers. 
 
 `` Callahan.'' 
 
 The SWAT guy gives me a handshake that crushes bones. He's a big guy. Gap toothed grin. 
 
 He introduces the rest, three more SWAT guys and a dozen beat cops. They're from the 1st and 5th Precincts. They bring gifts. 
 
 The trailer is loaded with weapons from evidence lockups and a shipment for destruction. They also stopped at a couple stores and picked up food. 
 
 Then he gets grim. 
 
 `` You got a major problem walking your way.'' He says. 
 
 `` Yeah, I heard, about two hundred idiots-'' 
 
 `` -you got some bad intel L.T. You got at least a thousand. They're hungry, scared, and some of them just want blood. They're about to start pouring in since the word got out. They've heard there's guns and food here.'' 
 
 Shit. 
 
 I excuse myself to radio the Major, stepping into the church. 
 
 There, in silence and alone, I vomit. 
 
 ***** 
 
 I step outside of the church, taking in the lowering sun. 
 
 The trailer is gone, along with most of the cops. Callahan and the SWAT guys stayed, bulking our manpower up. 
 
 I also see five guardsmen in full gear, a chunk of my missing NCOs. 
 
 `` Sir! We got caught trying to come in but we made it through, linked up with the Major and he sent us to you. He said that there's another platoon coming to reinforce, since a lot of refugees are saying a mob is headed our way.'' 
 
 Good news, I want to hug him but I do n't. 
 
 I check my watch again. 
 
 5:43 PM. 
 
 It's about to get dark. The power wo n't last much longer I expect, not with the riots and anyone who knows how to run a plant not exactly calling in to work. 
 
 Dark means trouble. 
 
 We have a handful of flares, not enough. 
 
 Out of all the concerns for the people in the city have, thinking their world is coming to an end, I have one myself. 
 
 Light. 
 
 There's shouting up the street. 
 
 My men are nervous and so am I. 
 
 `` Sir-'' Colville is quiet when he speaks, avoiding his voice carrying to the men, `` -we ca n't shoot Americans. They're just scared. They've lost everything. They think we wo n't bounce back from this.'' 
 
 He's right, we ca n't shoot them. Killing citizens? That's not our duty, our job. 
 
 `` Sergeant, we may not bounce back. The entire country is devolving into riots over food and water. FEMA and some guardsmen out in California were overrun and killed for two trucks worth of rations. It's only been two weeks since the market tanked, two fucking weeks! It's the same thing overseas. People are terrified, people are desperate. Sergeant, unless I'm mistaken we're people too. I'm more worried about the people who came to us for help than the people that want to take it by force.'' 
 
 He looks at me, nodding just slightly. He was with me. 
 
 We had people to protect. 
 
 Did that make us monsters? 
 
 I heard the shouting before I saw the crowd gathering, there were more than a thousand of them. They were forming a mob behind a garbage truck. 
 
 This was n't going to end well for a lot of people. 
 
 I felt my finger hammering against my rifle, making a clicking noise in the near silence of our defensive area. Everyone was looking to me. 
 
 Watching me. 
 
 It was a strange sense of calm that washed over me with a single realization. 
 
 We were going to survive. 
 
 The United States of America is dead. 
 
 We could restore something, some order or life to this place. At a price. 
 
 Blood.
retelling:
Character: **Sergeant Colville**

In the heart of New York City, on Malcolm X Boulevard and 111th Street, a small church stood as a beacon of hope amidst chaos. I, Sergeant Colville, found myself huddled within its walls, a seasoned soldier in a unit led by a young lieutenant who was navigating unfathomable circumstances. The southeast corner of the intersection became our defensive line against an enemy we barely knew.

Outside, the city screamed with despair and fury. Buildings burned, looting rampaged, and the once-bustling metropolis had transformed into a warzone. Amidst this devastation, we took refuge in the church, scavenging weapons from the Armory and supplies from wherever we could find them. The interior was cold and empty, yet it offered a modicum of protection against the madness outside.

The lieutenant had been tasked with establishing a perimeter around Central Park - a mission that seemed impossible given our limited numbers and resources. Our primary objective was to protect civilians caught in this maelstrom, but it was becoming increasingly difficult to tell friend from foe. We received intelligence of an approaching mob, far larger than any of us could have anticipated – thousands strong.

Despite the dire predictions, I could sense a determination burning within the lieutenant. He struggled with the thought of using force against desperate civilians, and rightly so. Yet he knew that we were their only protection, and he would not let them down. The darkness closed in around us, but still, he stood tall, ready to face whatever awaited us beyond those crumbling city streets.

As we braced ourselves for what was to come, I couldn't help but think about the world that had been lost. The United States of America as we once knew it was dying, and our survival effort now focused on holding onto every shred of hope we could find. The rioting started in Washington D.C., spreading like a cancer across the nation, and here we were, standing guard at a small church on the corner of Malcolm X Boulevard and 111th Street.

I looked around at my comrades, each one struggling with their own fears and doubts. But there was resolve in their eyes too - a determination to survive, to protect, and to hold onto whatever piece of humanity remained within us. I shared that resolve, for we were all soldiers now, fighting not for a flag or a country, but for the very survival of ourselves and those around us.

The tipped-over truck outside became our makeshift barrier and firing position. We fortified it as best we could, hoping it would be enough to hold against the onslaught that was surely coming. The streets beyond were empty now, filled only with the distant echoes of gunfire and sirens. But I knew they would soon be filled with the cries of the desperate and the dying.

As we stood there, waiting for dawn to break, I couldn't help but wonder what the future held for us. Would we survive this ordeal? Would the city be saved? Or would it collapse into chaos and despair? All I could do was focus on the task at hand, trusting that my fellow soldiers and I could hold onto hope, even as the darkness seemed to close in around us.

For now, we stood our ground, ready to face whatever came our way. The city outside may have been descending into chaos, but within those church walls, there remained a spark of defiance, a glimmer of hope that refused to be extinguished. And it was in that moment, as I looked around at my fellow soldiers, that I knew we would fight for every inch, for every life, and for the survival of our makeshift family.

name: DevinsCursedCoins
source:
A part of Devin's psyche, buried deep in his skull, nagged him during his shameful task. 
 
 
 He was sweeping a mantelpiece's contents into a pillowcase with a certain grace that comes with desperation and haste. As the picture frames and mementos clattered in the bottom, Devin worried that one of the pictures might have cracked. He stopped his pilfering and stood in the dark for a moment, and the adrenaline rush that came when he broke the door in subsided and his body shivered in shame. 
 
 
 He told himself this adolescent bullshit was for kids. He did stupid shit like this as a stupid child, and half of the reason why he was still considering this line of work was because of the stints in con college he enrolled in because of his childhood exploits. After the last row in Joliet, when his hair was still blonde and his face unmarred and smooth, he promised his brother he'd never steal again. 
 
 
 His brother was dead. Looking past his cheeks and past the lines that bore into them like the river deltas of Louisiana, you saw the somber eyes that never broke their gaze- the look of a man asking the world for a second chance that never seemed to come. 
 
 
 They were the eyes of a beggar. 
 
 
 
 
 Devin was still standing in that stranger's house, the hand clutching his bag of swag now loosening. For a moment, he heard his brother's shrill voice in his ear telling him he could still leave. 
 
 
 But he could n't. He had bills. Rent. Appearances to keep, minds to assuage, mouths to feed. Being on the bottom rung meant you could n't have high morals. 
 
 
 With that train of thought, a kind of pitiful sadness washed over Devin. It was the realization that he had resigned himself to a life of endless petty crime. With the cold making his bones shiver, he decided to make one last pass on the living room and leave before the cops arrived. 
 
 
 And that's when he saw it. A perfectly innocent water cooler jug, filled about a quarter of the way with spare change. It seemed below him. But, with his stomach pitted, he bitterly mused, `` Petty change for a petty thief,'' and threw the jug under his arm. 
 
 
 -- -- -- -- -- -- -- 
 
 
 
 He was back in the house in three hours. He was sweating so much he could n't grab the door handle. He was so nervous he did n't wear his gloves. 
 
 
 In his pockets, like a compass that led him back, were a handful of coins. There was no way for him to know it, but the random assortment he had taken back had weighed exactly ten grams. 
 
 
 Each coin drew Devin towards it; and in turn the coins drew him back to the house. When he got back to his house, for no reason at all he emptied the jug first. At first he thought it was to humiliate himself for taking such a tragic and ineffectual loot, but as he poured the change out his loathing turned into an unbridled curiosity that surprised him. 
 And when he glanced over the quarters he saw foreign faces. But when he inspected them they were indeed American currency- but impossible: mint dates long into the future. The next thing he knew he was already at the front door again with no memory of how he got there. 
 
 
 
 He carefully tread through the house. His hand still in his pocket, still clutching the miraculous money, he sat down in the kitchen and closed his eyes. 
 
 
 He was n't sure what he was doing. He was n't sure what was happening. He had planned to wait for the homeowners to return, to confront them, to find answers to the questions burning in his skull. But, when he closed his eyes, the warmth between each coin reverberated and shot up his arm and through his entire body. Sleep overcame him instantly, and he collapsed and fell on the ground. 
 -- -- -- -- -- -- - 
 
 
 He opened his eyes and was giving a speech to his high school class. He was in his underwear. The coins were still in his hands, now twice the size. He closed his eyes and saw the crowd from above, each person holding their own pair of coins glowing red hot. 
 
 
 He opened his eyes and was heating the coins in a strange laboratory. As he held a popsicle to the five coins, still in his hands, steam poured from the edges. The steam flooded the room, making the walls seems farther and farther away until he tried to reach out for them but found nothing for miles. 
 
 
 He opened his eyes, and found himself chained in a dark room the size of an outhouse. Above him lay a grate- big enough for a large 
 book to be lain across and block all the view of some sort of prison complex. Two sinister shadows suddenly appeared over the grate and Devin tried to recoil but was forced to meet their gaze. They muttered in vibrato and, when Devin swallowed his fear and called out to them, started to throw more coins into the trench. The coins were so hot every point of Devin they touched became engulfed in flames. He tried to scream but the fires stole his breath. He tried to struggle and climb over the coins, but failed. As the coins reached his chin, he cast one final look towards his specters. They were laughing. He closed his eyes and felt the coins burn a hole into his skull. 
 
 -- -- -- -- -- -- - 
 
 
 Devin woke up in the still-glowing embers of a frame of a house that had caught fire. His clothes were burnt to a crisp. Every breath filled him with pain- his ribs were broken. He was about four thousand miles from where he had found the coins; he slowly rose and found a clear night sky through the last piece of frame that still stood against gravity. The sky had stars unfamiliar to him. He was somewhere in the Nevada desert. 
 
 His right hand was still clutching something. All the blood was gone from it. His fingers were covered in burns, but he could n't feel anything. 
 
 He unfolded his fingers. A single coin remained. Any markings that made it distinguishable were now indeterminate. 
 But as he felt the coins between his fingers, he closed his eyes and heard a voice calling him. When he opened his eyes, he saw a glowing point on the horizon. 
 
 The voice had told him to follow the fires.

Narrative Perspective: The Specters/Shadows (Unnamed entities)

In the shadowy recesses of a realm beyond the mortal world, two spectral figures - timeless and eternal - observe with keen interest the happenings on Earth. On this particular occasion, their attention is drawn to a human named Devin, a thief who had ventured into the Stranger's House in Joliet.

From our vantage point, we see Devin as he prowls through the darkened halls and living room, his movements silent but for the soft creaking of the wooden floorboards underfoot. He is searching for something - a prize worth taking, a mark of his desperation. Unbeknownst to him, we watch as he stumbles upon an object that would change not only his life but our existence forever: a seemingly ordinary jug filled with coins, their dates far into the future.

We observe as Devin, filled with guilt and haunted by memories of his deceased brother, returns home to scrutinize the stolen coins. As he does so, we witness the strange effects that begin to take hold of him - visions, transformations, and a journey that would transport him across great distances.

From our spectral realm, we guide Devin through his trials, seeking to understand the purpose behind this human's possession of our coins. We watch as he endures the fiery ordeal in the Nevada desert, emerges battered but alive, and is guided by a voice towards a distant light.

As Devin clutches the altered coin in his hand, we sense a shift - a change in the balance of power between our world and theirs. We are compelled to follow this mortal's journey further, to learn more about these anomalous coins and the connection they seem to have with our realm.

In the dark corners of existence, we wait and watch, ready to intervene when necessary, as Devin continues to unravel the mystery that binds us together. Little do we know that this human's story will have far-reaching consequences for both our worlds.

name: FlorentineEscape
source:
Prologue 
 
 Firenze, Italia – Nov. 8th, 1494 
 
 She struggled to quicken her pace without drawing the attention of the city guard. A woman of her status was well known and observed; easily identified by anything more than a passing glance. Alfonsina Orsino had tucked her flaxen-colored hair beneath a frayed veil in hopes of distorting her appearance, but her skin was too pale; her posture too upright to pass off as a peasant. The drab gown borrowed from her handmaiden was lighter than the gold embroidered layerings she was used to, but in this moment she was grateful. Though the sweltering heat of the summer had long since cooled, in her haste the rising sun still brought sweat upon her brow. 
 
 As Alfonsina turned the corner into the bustling Piazza della Signoria, she held her breath deep within her chest. Though the noise came from directly in front of her, the deep toll of the bell tower shook the ground and reverberated from every direction. A flock of pigeons, startled from the rumbling, abandoned their nests atop the Torre d ’ Arnolfo. The chime, echoing throughout the city, summoned the citizens of Florence to the steps of the Palazzo Vecchio, the seat of government. 
 
 Men and women alike filtered into the square carrying weapons and yelling obscenities. Alfonsina scanned the crowd warily for a familiar face, but saw only cold hatred in the foreign eyes of the common people. Too long had they endured the extravagance of the Medici family as children starved in the streets; too long had they entrusted loyalty in a coward who had sold out their territories and their freedom to the invading French. They did not want Piero ’ s arrogant promises or semantics; they wanted Medici blood.

With furtive steps and downcast eyes, I darted through the labyrinthine city streets, desperate to evade recognition. Their hatred for the Medici family, our ruling dynasty, seethed beneath the surface, threatening to erupt at any moment like a cauldron boiling over.

As I approached Piazza della Signoria, my heart pounded in my chest like a drumbeat that echoed the rhythm of my thoughts - fear, anticipation, and the unmistakable thrill of danger. The square was abuzz with activity, the cobblestones reverberating beneath the footsteps of the angry mob that gathered at the very steps of Palazzo Vecchio.

The bell from Torre d'Arnolfo tolled, its mournful peal piercing the cacophony of voices raised in anger and defiance. The crowd surged forward, their weapons glinting menacingly in the fading sunlight as they converged upon the seat of our government.

I stood, frozen in place, my breath hitching in my throat as I bore witness to this uprising that threatened to shatter the very foundations of our city. My heart ached for Florence, for the people who suffered under the yoke of the Medici's rule, and for my own family whose fate hung precariously in the balance.

But amidst the chaos and uncertainty, I felt a flicker of hope. A spark that ignited within me the belief that change was possible, that we could rise from the ashes of our suffering and forge a new path for ourselves. name: AmnesiacCallCenterDevil
source:
When I woke up from a concussion-induced slumber, I did n't remember a thing about my past. Most of my knowledge stayed intact, but my memories vanished. Waking up, not knowing who you are, yet still knowing almost every single member of the Patriots is an odd feeling, as I'm sure you can imagine. If someone brought a gun to me, I could identify exactly what it was by name, yet I could n't remember my own. It was a strange time, if you have n't gotten that yet. 
 
 I woke up in an alleyway in New York City. I somehow knew the name of every street in the gigantic metropolis, and exactly what was on each one of those streets. Feeling sick from the concussion, I had to get to the nearest hospital. I followed my memory, and after traversing a couple of city blocks, I ended up at the local Catholic hospital, since that was the nearest one. 
 
 Naturally, they took me in immediately. The sisters there were great- they read stories to me from the Bible, treated my head injury, and, most importantly, set me up with a temporary job at the local parish to help me make money until my memory came back. 
 
 Life at the perish was incredible. I always had food to eat, the people were incredibly nice, I made a decent enough paycheck... But something about being there was just exhausting. I could go out with friends, do the heavy lifting on the church's mission trips, walk across the entire city... But something as simple as passing around the offering plate during Mass was fatiguing. 
 
 So I left. I hugged the sisters there that helped me get back on my feet, said goodbye to the friends I'd made, and found a new job. 
 
 It's fucking awful. I'm working at a call center for a large appliance manufacturer. Every single damned day I get the same calls... 
 
 `` My washing machine is n't cleaning my clothes!'' 
 
 `` Well, sir, walk me through how you wash your clothing.'' 
 
 `` Yeah, so I load the laundry. I turn it on. And when I pull the clothes out and dry them, they still stink and have stains in them!'' 
 
 `` You are using laundry detergent, right ( *you absolute fucking moron, I swear to Jesus, I want to shove you into your own washer and set it to'heavy load'* )?'' 
 
 Silence. Things like that. Every single day. People getting their cats stuck in the refrigerator. Asking why their microwave does n't work when they do n't even have it plugged in. And worst of all, no one is even grateful for when I solve their goddamned problems! 
 
 Today, I freaked out. I cursed this idiot out who got his freezer and fridge backwards and was n't sure why his milk kept freezing and his meat kept thawing. I said some absolutely awful things to him. I started calmly, but escalated, more and more and more until I was threatening to absolutely mutilate him. 
 
 And it felt good. I felt powerful. Everything felt right. That's what I was supposed to do. In the middle of threatening to chop him up and feed him to the pelicans on my back deck, I realized exactly what I've been missing. 
 
 You know that Satan guy your preacher warned you so much about? Yeah, he's real. And he just got fired from his job at a call center. And he's going to make you all pay for what you've turned him into.

name: ThirtyYearsThirtyLives
source:
Ten years I've been struggling to survive in this cursed chair. Ten long, agonizing years, as one bodily function after another shuts down. These days, I communicate one slow word at a time, translated ( or in this case, written down ) by the amazing, incredible love of my life. We met on my 30th birthday. She's stuck with me through all of this, the single, constant source of joy in my life. And nothing pains me more than knowing as I fall asleep, that tonight I wo n't wake up. I can tell that the end is upon me, and that I'll never again see her face or hear her voice again. 
 
 As I died, I woke up. Again, I thought? These dreams had been part of my life every six months or so since I was a child, but the frequency was increasing. Only a few standards existed between them -- nothing indicated I was dreaming. My life continued normally, in mundane detail, until the moment of my death, when I wake up back where I started ( plus or minus a few days -- still have n't quite figured out the break point there ). A few days to get used to having a young body again, after years of getting used to old age. And most importantly, on my 30th birthday, I meet her. The single, solitary, awesome constant through all the lives lived. The woman I love absolutely, unconditionally; the woman who makes any life worth living. 
 
 As I wipe the sleep from my eyes and start the process of settling back into my real body, my phone rings. It's my parents. I hit the answer button, put the phone to my ear, and almost immediately drop it in shock. My father has just asked me how it feels to have enjoyed 30 years on Earth. 
 
 By my reckoning, I have enjoyed closer to 3000. But none of them will compare to the joy of this day, when after so many centuries, I finally meet you in the flesh, when here, in reality, we can finally begin our lives together. I've waited so long for this moment. I have so much to tell you, my love.
retelling:
From the perspective of **The Narrator's Wife/Love**, we find ourselves embroiled in a captivating tale that spans epochs and transcends the boundaries of life and death.

For millennia, I have been her constant companion, my love for her as unwavering as the stars above. We met on her 30th birthday, our lives intertwining in an instant. The years that followed were marked by a dance between joy and sorrow, as she was afflicted by a condition that left her bound to a wheelchair, yet never diminishing my love for her.

In the vast expanse of time, I watched as she underwent a cycle that baffled comprehension. Ten years would pass, a lifetime in each iteration, and then, without warning, she was gone. But just as the sun rises after every night, so too did she reappear in another life, her spirit reborn anew.

I remember each encounter vividly - the raw pain of her absence, the heart-stopping moment of reunion, and the unspoken words that passed between us in those fleeting moments before we were torn apart once more. Yet with every cycle, there was a glimmer of hope - a promise that one day, our love would be free from this eternal dance.

As I stood by her side during each life, I could feel the weight of the years pressing down upon us. The phone call from her parents, confirming she had reached 30 in her current reality, was the culmination of a journey that had spanned countless lifetimes. With it came the realization that our love story was not confined to dreams and rebirths, but would finally unfold in the real world.

This tale is not just about a man who lived and died over and over again; it's about the love that endured through time itself. It's a testament to the power of connection and the promise of a future free from the cycle of death and rebirth, where we could finally live our lives together as intended. And so, I await the day when she will awaken in her final life, and we can experience the true meaning of love without the specter of mortality casting its long shadow over us.

name: RedHairedNord
source:
She comes in every day; The Nord woman with the short red hair and the daedrik armor. 
 
 Every day she brings in what I can only suppose are things stolen from houses and dragon dens. Normally I would shoo her away but, when she took off her helmet to ask me what I had for sale I relented. 
 
 I wanted to tell her that I think she is the most beautiful woman that I have ever seen, that over our countless encounters I have begun to fall in love with her. 
 
 But in my panic I can only muster up the courage to ask `` will you be needing anything else?'' 
 
 Damn my luck.
retelling:
From the Perspective of the Nord Woman:

In the heart of this bustling settlement, nestled between towering structures of stone and wood, lies a shop - a place where commerce thrives and goods change hands. This is where I frequent, a place run by a man whose gaze lingers longer than necessary upon me each time I enter. He's a small, timid creature with an air of anxiety that seems to perpetually cling to him like a second skin. Today, however, something felt different.

I had just returned from another successful expedition, the weight of my loot - dragon scales and treasures from ancient tombs - pulling at my leather belt. As I stepped into his dimly lit store, the familiar scent of dried goods and worn armor filled my nostrils. The man's eyes widened in surprise, his gaze tracing the lines of my Daedric armor as if he could uncover its secrets through mere observation.

I approached his counter, my heart pounding with a mixture of anticipation and trepidation. He looked up at me then, his blue eyes peeking out from beneath a fringe of disheveled hair. His gaze lingered upon my face for an unusually long moment before dropping back to the items I'd brought. I knew what he was thinking; he suspected that my goods were stolen. But today, I decided to play along.

With a slow, deliberate motion, I lifted my helmet from my head and set it on the counter. My red hair cascaded down my back like a river of flame, catching his eyes and holding them captive. His breath hitched in his throat, and for a moment, I thought he might say something - anything - but instead, he mumbled a polite greeting and began the tedious process of assessing my goods.

His hands shook as he handled each item, his nerves plainly on display. I couldn't help but smile at his discomfort, enjoying the power I held over him. As he weighed the dragon scales and inspected the trinkets, I allowed myself to drift back to that night - the night I'd fought the dragon and claimed its hoard as my own. The adrenaline still pulsed through my veins, a constant reminder of my strength and cunning.

I left his shop that day with more than just coin in my purse. I left with the knowledge that I held sway over this man, and that was far more valuable than any hoard of dragon treasure. And so, each time I returned to his shop, I would play my part - the thief who could charm her way out of trouble - because it was a game I enjoyed playing, and he was always eager for his next turn.

name: FinalBirthTunnel
source:
Finally. After so long. 
 
 I can feel it. 
 
 There's a squeezing feeling. Like my whole body is being sent through some sort of tunnel. It's hard to describe, you'd have to experience it for yourself. There's the pounding of the blood, and yes, the sounds of someone wailing, faint to my ears, but there, nonetheless. 
 
 Yes. I can feel it. Today's the day. My long journey is almost over. 
 
 I have been waiting for so many days and weeks and months now. Trapped in my body. Trapped in place. Useless. 
 
 But today... I will be freed from the shackles life had placed upon me. 
 
 I wonder what is out there, once I'm gone from this prison, and what awaits me. 
 
 My god... my head, it's KILLING me... But... wait.. what's this? A light? At the end of a tunnel? 
 
 And I'm moving towards it! 
 
 Wow. I never thought it would look like that. So bright! It's... beautiful... 
 
 I want to whimper, but now the tightness has it's firm grip upon me, and I can hardly make a peep! Please... please, let it be over soon... 
 
 Wait! What's happening? I'm... I'm losing myself! I ca n't... remaremer... remamler... NO! *Remember! * 
 
 I have so much to do! So much to pass on! I ca n't... I ca n't... the light... I'm... i.. 
 
 NO! I... *MUST*... remem... ber... 
 
... 
 
. 
 
 -- - 
 
 `` Congratulations!'' said the doctor, as he held up the newest member of the Berkston family. `` It's a boy!''

   The newest member of the Berkston family, a small, wriggling bundle swathed in white, lies on the table before me, his face bruised and wet from his journey into the world. His mother, exhausted yet radiant, looks up at me with eyes full of gratitude and relief.

   I see the narrator, unseen but not unnoticed, standing near the door. Their expression is a mask of tension and anxiety, their eyes fixed on us – the stage and the players in this dramatic event. They feel trapped by their role as observer, their heart pounding in sync with the baby's. Yet, they sense a glimmer of hope, a promise of liberation that the arrival of this child brings.

   The sensations I am experiencing are vastly different from those of the narrator. Here, in the realm of medical science, I feel powerful and purposeful. My hands move with precision as I examine the baby, checking for vital signs, ensuring he is strong enough to face the world outside the womb.

   Suddenly, the room is filled with a wailing sound – the baby's cry echoing off the cold, white walls. It's a symphony of life, the sweetest music I know, and it signals that all is well. I look up at the narrator, my eyes meeting theirs for a fleeting moment before I return to my task. In that instant, I see their relief mirrored in mine.

   With one final glance at the family, I step back, allowing them their privacy as they begin this new chapter of their lives together. I turn and leave the delivery room, the baby's cries fading behind me, replaced by the steady hum of life that fills the hospital. And though the narrator remains in the background, a silent witness to life's miracles, today, they too have been freed – free to bear witness to the wonders of new beginnings.

name: ericMayaGhost
source:
`` SON OF A BITCH!'' Eric all but roared as he kicked the door of it's rusty hinges. 
 
 `` Eric you need to calm down, you're freaking me out.'' Maya said from behind him. `` Please put the knife down.'' She asked, tears starting to form in her eyes. 
 
 `` No!'' He yelled turning back toward her `` She's here! Ca n't you see her?'' He demanded. His eyes were filled with a horrible combination of terror and rage, but his knife hand was steady as he turned back to the room he had just kicked open. The woman inside had moved. 
 
 Not a lot, perhaps a foot from the spot she had been, but she was closer now. The shadows on her face a stark contrast to light coming from her eyes. Seeing her again filled Eric with so much terror he would have run screaming from this damned house if it was n't for his rage. She looked at him, she looked at him, and she grinned. 
 
 Seeing that sent Eric back in time, to waking up at night in the orphanage, with her standing over him and Sarah. To when they first got adopted, and they saw her in every mirror of the house. To when that house burned down with their foster parents inside, and all they could see was her in the doorway with that horrible grin on her face. To when Sarah died in a car crash, after swerving to avoid a pedestrian that was never there. To last night, when he had gone to check on his son, and found HER grinning over the crib. So he had come back. 
 
 `` Hello Eric.'' Her lips never moving, but he heard it, coming from all around him, a whisper from the shadows nearly driving him to his knees. He looked back up at her, but she was gone. He spun around and there she was, her eyes filling his vision. He did not think, his body took over, relying on instinct, he plunged the knife forward, straight into her stomach. 
 
 `` Hello Mother.'' He whispered as he pulled the knife out and looking her right in those horrible eyes, thrust it back in, up to to the hilt. 
 
 He blinked and she was gone. No sound, no light, just... gone. He had a second of pure joy, that he was safe, that Maya and James could finally be safe. He closed his eye and sent a silent thanks to the God he did not believe in. Then he remembered that he had not seen Maya in the room. That was when he heard the body hit the floor. 
 
 He did n't want to open his eyes, did n't want to see what his mind could not process. He opened them slowly, and saw her. His Maya, on the floor, covered in her own blood, she looked at him, with confusion and pain in her eyes. Her breathing turned into a coughing fit, and then she was gone, leaving behind a broken man and a bloody corpse. 
 
 The knife slipped out of his hand as he fell to his knees. `` No.'' He whispered, as the tears came. `` No. No. No.'' He whispered over and over again. 
 
 `` Yes.'' Whispered the shadows. Suddenly she was there, her grin wider then before, stretching across her entire face. They stayed like that for what seemed like an eternity, before she made one small movement. She held the knife out to him, hilt first. His hand's shaking, he reached out slowly and took it.
retelling:
Narrative Perspective: Maya

   In the dimly lit recesses of a decaying house, I found myself huddled with Eric, a man grappling with ghosts from his past that threatened to consume us both. The air was thick with tension and foreboding, the rusty hinges on the door groaning as if in protest to our intrusion.

   Eric's eyes were wild, his grip on the knife he had brought tightening around mine as we ventured further into the darkness. His tales of a spectral woman haunting him, causing tragedy after tragedy, seemed far-fetched, yet I couldn't deny the fear that gnawed at my heart.

   We entered a room, its shadowy corners concealing secrets we dared not guess. Eric, in his determination to confront this apparition, lunged forward, the knife he brandished glinting ominously in the sparse light. I screamed as he struck out, the sound echoing through the house like a mournful wail.

   The entity, if it truly was one, remained unseen, its presence felt only in the chilling breeze that swept through the room and the palpable fear that coursed through Eric's veins. I wished I could have believed in his story, that our shared past as orphans, living under the cold gaze of the same orphanage, had somehow bound us to this specter.

   But the entity was not done with us. As Eric fell to his knees, blood streaming from a shallow wound on his arm, I beheld the sight that would haunt me for the rest of my days: the woman standing over him, offering him the very knife he had used in his futile attempt at vengeance.

   In that moment, I knew there was no escape. No amount of love or understanding could shield us from this relentless specter. All I could do was hold Eric as his life slipped away, whispering words of comfort and love into the echoing silence.

   The entity reappeared, her gaze lingering on me for a moment before fading back into the shadows. I could feel its malevolent presence, a cold weight pressing down on my chest, suffocating any hope I once harbored. And so, in that dilapidated house, the story of Eric and the ghostly woman came to its tragic end.

name: NebulonTerrierIncident
source:
I look down at the little Terrier and smile, `` Yes. Now, who's a good dog? Who's a good dog?!'' 
 
 The blonde pup growls at me and gets itself up on his hind two legs like an adorable, little cinnamon roll. It climbs up to my shoulders, arms reached out and holding on, and stares into my eyes. 
 
 `` I'll have you know, human girl. I am a Rootebegan Zingtiter from Nebulon-336. I graduated at the top of my class in biological studies, researched countless diseases, and ended the plague on Zentyrion-540 within a fortnight. And thus, I will NOT be disrespected as one of your common Sol-42 mutts!'' 
 
 I smile and grab onto its cute, hairy face, poking my index finger at its nose. 
 
 `` You are! You're a good doggy!'' 
 
 It snarls at me, that Terrier, before something stirs inside its heart and it starts lapping at my face. `` I am! I'm a good boy!'' 
 
 Immediately, I pull out my phone and take a picture of the the two of us on the bus. My hand pets its wittle head the whole time as it continues to bark lovingly with English words. 
 
 `` Yes, you are!'' I repeat to it, `` Yes, you are!'' 
 
 Unfortunately, I'm immediately detained by the Ape security guards patrolling the tour bus and thrown into the airlock seconds after for sexually harassing a member of a foreign species in a public area. There's a big news scandal back at home regarding the matter, along with a proposal from the United Galaxies to lock down Human migration into their zones. 
 
 I do n't care. I took pictures of that adorable puppy and I'm proud of it.

Initially, the vibrant energy that emanated from this being was overwhelming, but my curiosity superseded my apprehension.

   I am Rootebegan Zingtiter, a terrier-like alien dog hailing from Nebulon-336, a planet rich in history and advanced technology. The tales of my heroic act on Zentyrion-540, where I ended a deadly plague, still echo in the cosmos. Yet, here I was, far from home, trying to navigate this new environment while maintaining a semblance of dignity.

   As I sat in my designated area, a soft, warm hand reached towards me, sending jolts of surprise coursing through my cybernetic limbs. The being's eyes widened with excitement, and I recoiled, trying to maintain my distance. But the scent of fear that wafted from her was comforting, reminding me of the humans who once cared for me back on Nebulon-336.

   Over time, I succumbed to the gentle affection she displayed, and we formed an unexpected bond. However, as the bus rolled through the starry skies, little did I know that this connection would lead to a storm of controversy and misunderstanding.

   The next thing I knew, Ape security guards were looming over me, their imposing figures casting long shadows. They accused me - or rather, her - of inappropriate advances. I could sense the confusion and despair emanating from my friend, as well as the bitter taste of betrayal.

   News of this scandal spread like wildfire, tarnishing my reputation and igniting a debate over human-alien interactions. Restrictions on human migration were imposed, leaving me stranded in a place far away from home. Despite the consequences, I remain grateful for the brief moments we shared, and the memories of her gentle touch will forever be etched in my circuitry.

name: gelliusBathDeath
source:
Based on all the representations of the Afterlife that Gellius had encountered during his lifetime, none had prepared him for the truth. The Afterlife was, for the lack of a better word, just your average bathroom. In the large cast iron bathtub sat Death. He lazily pushed a skeletal rubber ducky with a boney finger. *Vroomsh! * noises rolled out of his lipless mouth. 
 
 `` Is this hell?'' Gellius asked visibly uncomfortable. `` Because I ca n't imagine it being Heaven. Sorry.'' Gellius always made a point of being polite. 
 
 `` Oh, no,'' Death replied, dunking the rubber ducky under the water. It returned to the surface with a refreshing *plop*. `` I just needed a bath. I played chess with Pestilence. Last time I did that was in 1347 and I did n't take a bath afterwards. Well... Let's just say it meant working overtime. You'll know all that stuff soon enough, though.'' 
 
 `` What?'' 
 
 `` Yeah, did n't Peter tell you? You've been assigned to replace me. According to Anu and Muhammed, who are chairing the Committee for the Replacement of the Representation of Death, you were the ideal candidate.'' 
 
 Gellius chuckled. He was not surprised to hear this. Being dead certainly changed your perspective on things. He was, however, very much confused by all of this. 
 
 `` Anu? Muhammed? Committee? Is this the part where you reveal to me that all the myths, legends and faiths are true, *and* the Afterlife is run like a failing corporation?'' 
 
 Death pondered this for a moment while splashing the water - making waves for the ducky to ride. 
 
 `` No. Not *all* the myths are true. Jesus' body is not present in the bread, nor is his blood present in the wine. That's really dumb. Scientology only has it partly right.'Xenu' did not do all those things. Tom Cruise did.'' 
 
 `` *What. *'' 
 
 `` Yeah, y'know. The Eternal Return of Zeus, Christ, Cruise.'' Death let out something resembling a sigh as he stood up, using a blanket to cover his modesty had he had any. Still dripping, he carefully stepped out of the tub. 
 
 `` Look,'' he continued. `` The moment you take over, it will all make sense to you...'' 
 
 `` But I do n't *want* to be Death!'' Gellius interjected. Certainly he would have a say in the matter? 
 
 `` I guess, but you also did not want to die. And that happened. So, yeah...'' 
 
 `` That makes no sense!'' interjected Gellius again, this time more fiercely. 
 
 `` I guess. Or rather... Not yet, anyway. Look, you have been selected for the job, and it really is interesting. Omnipresence is not something you humans get to experience all that often. You'll go places. Meet people. The secondary benefits are *o-kay*. Unless they changed the contract, you can overturn Destiny and/or Chance thrice a century. Quite a blast. Also, you'll know *The Truth*, about *Everything*.'' 
 
 Gellius' mind raced as his eyes scanned the bathroom. The shower curtain had a pink'Hello Skully' pattern. Accepting the fact he had no say in the matter, Gellius turned his attention back to Death, who was drying his bones with a rose-coloured towel. 
 
 `` Well, alright. Just one question...'' 
 
 `` Shoot. We have all eternity.'' 
 
 ``... What? Err... Right. Omnipresence. Anyway, is the skeletal'Grim Reaper' thing mandatory?'' 
 
 Death shook his skull. 
 
 `` Nah. You'll be the representation of Death, but how you represent yourself is up to you. One of the perks. My predecessor did the perky, sexy goth girl thing. Her predecessor always took the form of the deceased's loved ones.'' 
 
 `` How did your predecessor be a goth girl if you've been working since the 14th century?'' 
 
 `` Omni-'' 
 
 ``... presence, right. Got it. I think.'' 
 
 By now Death had put on his robes. 
 
 `` Ready?'' He asked. 
 
 `` I guess?'' 
 
 Death simply nodded. Extending a bony finger, he touched Gellius' forehead. And that was that.
retelling:
Narrated by **Death**, the enigmatic being who has decided it's time for a change:

In the quiet and ordinary sanctuary of an average bathroom, bathed in a soft pink light from a 'Hello Skully' patterned shower curtain, I found myself in the midst of preparing to retire. A simple task, one that has been repeated countless times over the millennia, yet today held a unique twist - the selection of my successor.

As I submerged myself in the warm waters of the cast iron bathtub, I felt a familiar presence - Pestilence, my perpetual chess partner and confidant. We had played across the ages, our games marking significant events in history. But today was not for games; today, I was here to pass on the mantle of Death.

With a sense of foreboding, I called forth Peter, a messenger with whom I've shared many a secret. He delivered the news that would change the lives of both Gellius and myself - Gellius had been chosen as my successor. The decision had not been made lightly; it was the result of careful deliberations by members of the Committee for the Replacement of the Representation of Death, including Anu and Muhammed.

As I explained to Gellius the responsibilities that would accompany his new role, I felt a pang of regret. Not all religious myths were true, as he would soon learn. Myths about Jesus, Tom Cruise, Scientology's Xenu, even the "Eternal Return" - none of these stories held the truth. But this was not something to be mourned; it was a testament to the boundless imagination and creativity of humanity.

Gellius, initially hesitant, ultimately accepted his fate. With newfound understanding that he had some freedom in how he would represent Death, he agreed to take on the role. As I appointed him my successor, I knew that this ordinary bathroom was not just a humble space but the gateway to the universe itself. The vastness of places he would visit as the new representation of Death stretched before me like an endless sea of possibilities.

And so, with a heart full of both nostalgia and anticipation, I bid farewell to my role as the embodiment of Death, leaving behind a world that would forever be entwined with the echoes of our shared history.

name: ShipwreckedGenieWish
source:
A man falls off a boat in a storm and washes up on a deserted beach where he finds a lamp sticking out of the sand. 
 
 Figuring `` Why the hell not?'' the man rubs the lamp and sure enough out pops this super hot female genie. The man ca n't believe his incredible luck. 
 
 `` Greetings, Master,'' she says. `` I will grant you whatever you wish, whether it is incredible wealth, love, long life, or all these things. Just know there are two rules.'' 
 
 `` Rule one: I am very generous. There is no need to wish for unlimited wishes. I will grant you everything you desire. You have only to rub my lamp once before each wish.'' 
 
 `` And rule two?'' asked the man. 
 
 `` Rule two: I'm kind of a bitch. I will grant your wish only as the words come out of your mouth, so be careful how you word them. You never know what you might get. So what is your first wish?'' 
 
 The man stops and thinks to himself `` I can have whatever I want. Money, fame, power, lots of beautiful women. I just have to outsmart her so she also grants my wish as I want it... That's it!'' 
 
 The man smiles. `` Genie, for my first wish I want to be the smartest man in the world!'' 
 
 The Genie nods her head and poof the man turns in Stephen Hawking.
retelling:
Narrative Perspective: The Female Genie

In the realm of lamps, I, the female genie, have been trapped for millennia, waiting for my freedom to be granted by the one who rubs me. My existence is defined by the power bestowed upon me and the wishes that bring about change in the world outside my confines.

One stormy day, as a tempest churned the sea, I felt the familiar vibration of the earth shaking beneath my lamp's pedestal. A man, driven by the fury of the waves, fell from his boat and washed ashore. His fate was to find me, the one who could change his life in an instant.

The man, shivering and drenched, discovered the lamp that lay half-buried on the deserted beach. With trembling hands, he rubbed my surface, releasing me from my eternal slumber. I appeared before him, my form a reflection of his deepest desires - clothed in flowing robes, with skin as dark as the midnight sky and eyes aglow with cosmic fire.

"I am granted one wish," the man said, his voice quivering with anticipation. "I wish to be the smartest man in the world."

The request was clear, yet there was something within his plea that made me pause. I could sense his longing for knowledge, for understanding of the universe's mysteries. But as a genie bound by my nature, I must grant wishes exactly as they are asked.

With a deep breath, I spoke, "By your wish, you shall be known as Stephen Hawking, and your intellect will surpass that of any who have come before or will follow after."

The man's eyes widened with shock and disbelief at the transformation that unfolded before him. His body contorted in ways I could not comprehend, his voice altered to a weak whisper. Yet, there was no regret in his gaze - only determination to use his newfound knowledge to unravel the secrets of the universe.

And so, as he walked away from the beach, leaving me once more alone in my lamp, I couldn't help but wonder if I had granted a wise wish or one that would bring about consequences neither of us could foresee. Yet, such is the nature of wishes, and the power that comes with being a genie.

reasoning.consistency: While the retelling maintains the core plot elements from the original story, it also adds nuance by exploring the Genie's thoughts and motivations. This demonstrates a solid understanding of the original story and its themes.
reasoning.retelling_depth: The retelling delves deep into the Female Genie's character, exploring her emotions, thoughts, and motivations. It also shows an understanding of the man's character and his desires, adding depth to the retelling.

name: woodsBodyMystery
source:
Noah Austin sat in the breakroom, coffee cup in one hand, folded newspaper in the other. Brown eyes focused, with a slight line on his forehead from concentration. Bianca Wilkinson shimmied her shirt slightly lower than she would dare to wear it in the classroom, fixed her cherry lipstick, and slipped into the chair next to Noah. *He could be a GQ model, * she smiled, “ Hi Noah ”. Much to her chagrin, Noah ’ s eyes remained downcast on the newspaper, lips pressed in a frown. 
 
 “ Is everything alright? ” Bianca tried again to draw his attention. 
 
 “ Hmm? ” He looked up from the paper, slightly confused. “ Oh, um, yeah. Yeah, ” He shook his head slightly. 
 
 “ You sure? ” Bianca leaned in slightly, looking at the article he had been reading. It was about the body found in the woods last week. A cause of death had been determined. “ An *animal* attack? ” It was her turn to frown. 
 
 “ So they say, ” Noah handed her the paper. Bianca pushed her hair back and began to read the rest of the article. “ Still no ID on the victim though. ” 
 
 “ Must ’ ve been from the city, ” Bianca suggests, “ It always surprises me how many people don ’ t know that we get wild animals along the river ’ s edge. ” 
 
 “ That ’ s true. Still. It ’ s the third death in as many months... And an animal attack too. Something just seems... *off* about the whole situation, ” Noah leaned into the paper again. Bianca turned to look at Noah, to see the gears turning behind his soft brown eyes. He brought his gaze up to meet hers, but not without lingering a moment to long on her lips. 
 
 He shook his head slightly. “ Hey, but I ’ m sure the police have got it. This town is no stranger to strange things after all. ” He chuckled softly to himself, “ But, uh, Bianca, I ’ ve been meaning to ask you. Do you maybe wan na go - ” 
 
 “ Talking about the body in the woods, are you? ” Bianca and Noah ’ s heads swiveled around to the unwelcome intrusion. Malcolm McCoy, the ancient biology teacher stood at the coffee pot. His wiry grey hair stood out in every direction. His wide frame glasses ( which Bianca suspected were actually from the 80s, not just made to look it ) made his grey eyes unnervingly large. “ Because I ’ ll tell you - it ’ s just the *weirdest* thing, ” he sat next to Bianca and Noah, unaware of what he had just interrupted. “ Last week that Peterson girl - Diana, I think- bombarded me with questions all week about the local fauna. I ’ m glad the girl is finally paying attention to something; she ’ s always off in her daydreams, that one. But the sudden interest in hunting patterns? I even told her wolves have n't been sighted in the area for years, but she would not let it go, that stubborn girl. It ’ s just so strange, given everything that ’ s been happening. ” 
 
 “ Oh I wouldn ’ t give it too much thought, ” Bianca brushed off Malcolm. “ Diana ’ s always been odd. Just last month she came to me asking for books about vampires. And not, like, fictional books - she wanted to know the history of the myths. All the way back, further than even the medieval history, right down to the Ancient Greek roots. I asked if she was a *Twilight* fan and she just rolled her eyes at me. Apparently, ‘ that ’ s so 2007, Miss Wilkinson. ’ ” 
 
 Noah chuckled while Malcolm just looked vaguely confused as to what *Twilight* was and why it was outdated. “ I think I can oneup both of you, ” he smiled and raised an eyebrow as if to say *you won ’ t believe this*. “ So it was my first week here, after Jenn left on her stress leave partway through the semester. I was laying down the rules, and the *first* thing she did -when I asked if there were any questions- was to stick up her hand and ask me about the *physics of magic*. At first I thought she was joking, but no, she just stared me down while the rest of the class laughed. ” 
 
 Bianca laughed at Noah ’ s story. “ See what I mean? ” She directed her statement towards Malcolm, “ Strange girl - no doubt - but she ’ s hardly dangerous. Probably just watching too much *Buffy*. ” 
 
 Noah smiled at Bianca, “ Now if the students think *Twilight* is an outdated reference, wait until they hear that one. ” She rolled her eyes with mock indignation.
retelling:
Narrated by Malcolm McCoy, the biology teacher:

In the familiar confines of the school breakroom, I find myself engrossed in my daily ritual - reading the local newspaper over a steaming cup of coffee. The usual chatter and laughter fill the air, but today's headline about another body found in the woods near the river demands my full attention. Ruled an animal attack? I can't help but feel uneasy as I recall similar incidents happening within the past few months.

A moment later, Noah Austin, the history teacher, enters the room, his eyes glued to the same article. We exchange a knowing glance before delving into the details of the grim discovery. Bianca Wilkinson, the English teacher, joins us soon after, her curiosity piqued by the mystery that surrounds this death.

As we discuss the peculiarities of the case, I can't help but be reminded of a recent encounter with one of my students - Diana Peterson. She had been particularly interested in our school's local fauna, asking detailed questions about hunting patterns and behaviors. Her queries were so specific and intense that they left me feeling a bit unsettled.

Bianca shares a similar experience, revealing that Diana had also bombarded her with books on vampire mythology. The strange coincidence between our experiences doesn't escape either of us, but Bianca dismisses it as mere eccentricity. I can't help but wonder if there is more to this young woman than meets the eye.

Lost in thought, my attention drifts towards Noah, who is now discussing Diana's questions about the physics of magic. It seems that our student has a penchant for the unusual and supernatural. The pieces begin to fall into place - a murder mystery, an enigmatic student, and an eerie connection between them all. As the day unfolds, I can't shake off this feeling of unease, sensing that the school breakroom might not be the only setting in which this story will continue to unfold.
