name: GuardianAngelsMarioKart
source:
Walking in to my house I knew something was awry. Three unicorns parked outside my house, eating my grass, and shitting all over my yard. My front door, which leads directly to my living room, was unlocked, welcoming me to another boring couple of hours in what I call'my life'. `` Honey, I'm home!'' I shout sarcastically. Three angels sitting in my living room - their faces painted eager. `` Sit down, Mitchell. We have much to discuss.'' 
 
 This has happened before. These three bores turn up like clockwork trying to get me to alter my lifestyle. A lifestyle I very much enjoy, I should add. Angel Clive, one of the first angels to ever take an interest in me, removes a large slab of stone from the inside of his robe and holds it high above his head like Link finding a sword for the first time. A small red dot appears on the stone pointing towards the first inscription:'I am the Lord thy God.' It's Dave the Angel with his laser pen. 
 
 `` First thing's first, I'm the realest.'' exclaims Dave, much to the enjoyment of the other angels. `` You know, like Iggy Azalea? It's like Iggy Azalea, Mitchell.'' 
 
 Welcome, everybody. This is the reality of having Guardian Angels. 
 
 `` As you know by now, rule # 1 must always be announced and understood before proceedings can, well, proceed. God is life. God is eternal. God is love.'' All three angels gently sweep the floor with their right hand, make a cross on their chests, kiss their fingers and point towards the sky. Every sportsman has got this spot on by the way. I have no idea how. 
 
 The laser pointer moves down. `` # 2, Mitchell.'Thou shalt have no other gods before me'. We have gone through this before so why do you still insist on calling yourself the'God of Mario Karts'? 
 
 `` Pick up that pad and I'll show you'' 
 
 Angel John motioned to pick up the pad. He always does. He's like that one friend who, even though he knows he is going to be beaten in to furious rage, he will always play. 
 
 `` Angel John, no! His Rainbow Road game is too strong, we have been witness to this in the past. Whilst we acknowledge your prowess we must insist you drop the'God' title from your nickname. It says right here on this large slab of stone that you are n't allowed to do that. Do I require a larger laser pointer?'' 
 
 `` I'm not dropping the God moniker until John over there picks up the pad and beats me'' 
 
 Angel John instantly goes for the pad. `` JOHN, I SAID NO!'' bellows Angel Dave. 
 
 The laser pointer shoots down to the inscription'Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy'. `` May I ask, Mitchell, just how have you been keeping the sabbath day holy?'' 
 
 `` I have n't. I'm not even sure how to keep the sabbath day holy.'' 
 
 `` He's not sure how to keep the sabbath day holy. Angel Clive, enlighten Mitchell for me, please'' 
 
 Angel Clive, still holding the heavy slab of stone above his head, looked a little puzzled. `` Well, on the seventh day God rested. Which was good. So I rest too. Bit of Playstation 4 and just pig out. I really like the HD remake of The Last of Us.'' 
 
 Angel Dave looked bemused. `` Are you fucking kidding, Angel Clive?'' Yes the Last of Us HD remake was very, very good but we are n't here to discuss Playstation 4. We're here to make Mitchell a better person. Just start keeping the sabbath day holy. Go to church or something. MOVING ON.'' 
 
 Out of the corner of my eye I can see John now has hold of the GameCube pad he was denied earlier on. `` I know you can hear me, Mitchell. I'm a fucking Angel. Telepathy is one of my many talents. I'm going to wreck you on Karts the second this farce of an intervention finishes. I'll be playing the harp for the final lap such will be the magnitude of my destruction. Eternal damnation via the power of red shells..'' 
 
 Angel Dave interrupts ``.. Angel John, we can all hear everything you're saying to Mitchell telepathically. We are Angels too. We have identical powers. He beats you every time you play him.'' 
 
 “ This time will be different ” 
 
 “ It ’ s never different, Angel John. You play, you get beat, you say the game is fake and then go home.'' 
 
 `` I do n't want to hold the slab anymore'' admits Angel Clive. 
 
 `` You see what you have caused, Angel John? Now Angel Clive does n't want to hold the slab anymore. Can you remember how long it took us to convince him to hold the slab?'' 
 
 `` I just want one shot at him on Rainbow Road.'' adamantly states Angel John. 
 
 `` Fine. Boot the GameCube up. But after the God of Karts beats you we are going through the Commandments again.'' 
 
 
 -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- - 
 
 This is one of my first times posting to /r/writingprompts. I'm not sure how serious the replies are supposed to be but I hope a stupid short story about an intervention turning in to a Mario Kart challenge is OK.
retelling:
Narrated by Angel Dave:

From my ethereal vantage point, I watched over Mitchell, the self-proclaimed "God of Mario Karts," as he went about his daily life, oblivious to the divine intervention that was about to unfold. Alongside my fellow angels, Clive and John, we had been assigned to guide him towards a more righteous path.

The day began with an unusual sight: three unicorns grazing in Mitchell's yard, a clear sign of his neglect for the world around him. We entered through the unlocked front door, stepping into the cluttered living room that was home to countless Mario Kart paraphernalia.

Clive, our most diplomatic angel, approached Mitchell with a stone tablet inscribed with the Ten Commandments, aiming to remind him of his duty to honor and respect the divine. However, our mission soon took an unexpected turn when John suggested a rematch, reigniting their long-standing rivalry on the Mario Kart tracks.

I attempted to steer the conversation back to its original course, reminding John of the importance of our objective. But it seemed as though my laser pointer was more captivating to him than the path to enlightenment. As the arguments escalated, it became clear that we were far from achieving our goal.

In a moment of desperation, I brought up Iggy Azalea, hoping her name would serve as a distraction and remind Mitchell of his earthly responsibilities. But alas, even the mention of the talented rapper failed to derail John's persistent desire for another Mario Kart race.

Reluctantly, we agreed to let Mitchell prove his skills on the track one more time, with the understanding that our spiritual discussion would resume afterward. As I looked into Mitchell's determined eyes, I could not help but feel a glimmer of hope that perhaps, one day, he might find the path to redemption and become the righteous Mario Kart champion we all knew he could be.

name: ReturnSignalContact
source:
`` Wow'' he exclaimed, circling a seemingly random jumble of characters in a long string of letters and numbers, even going so far as to write the word down on the margin of the printout. 
 
 `` What is it?'' said Jane, his faithful assistant. She'd been there with him through all the boring nights, all the fruitless searches. She knew there was something on that page that required attention. If it got him to say something out loud, to break that interminable silence that made up their nightly routine, it must have been special. She quelled her excitement, not wanting to raise the tension in the room. Years they'd been looking at empty sky for something, anything. 
 
 `` I do n't know for sure, let's run a few more sweeps across sector X-52. I want to make sure this is n't an anomaly before getting my hopes up.'' He quickly slid his chair across the room and began furiously turning dials and entering coordinates on a dim screen. 
 
 `` It had better not be nothing'' she thought silently to herself. 
 
 `` The first words he utters related to something coming out of this fucking antenna array that are n't bitching about funding and he wants to double check?'' Her frustration was growing. `` No, he's right'' her mind raced. `` Just double check...'' 
 
 `` Holy Shit Jane. Holy Shit. You've got to see this, make sure I'm not crazy or dreaming'' He spun around in his chair and tossed her a second printout. 
 
 There it was. A signal. Standing out like a candle in a closet. It could n't be missed. Absolutely stunning... she had her ideas for what came next, but she was the junior on this project. `` OK Tom, now what do we do with it? This is amazing, it's going to change everything. Well, it could... no it definitely will. I ca n't belie...'' She was cut off by Tom grabbing the printout and dashing out of the stale dark room. 
 
 `` SCAN IT AGAIN! Do not turn off anything! Get a secondary backup going'' he yelled as he ran out into the hall to make the phone call that she knew was coming. Tom had the prestigious honor of waking up the President. It was after all the protocol which had been established back when this project was first set in motion, long before public interest had faded, long before funding was being strung along on a weekly basis. 
 
 Water on Europa. Bacteria on Mars. Single celled organisms on that asteroid... life was everywhere. That's why we sent them in there. They were to go through the wormhole which appeared just outside the bounds of Jupiter's orbit and if possible, report back on what they had found. 100 years had passed since they left the Earth. And now, just now, a ray of hope. There's intelligent life out there - because we sent it there. 
 
 They were trying to reach us. Wherever we sent them, they were somehow able to reach back across the void to let us know they were ok. The radio signature was unmistakable, that was for sure. What was strange was the intensity, the regularity, the absolutely staggering range that the signal was beginning to encompass. 
 
 It was coming through on multiple frequencies now - radio, microwave, infrared, literally everything was reading the same thing. There was certainly no point in being cautious with informing the powers-that-be. Even the television was playing the signal. In the 5 minutes it took for the first pings to come through until now the signal had grown in scope to encompass every means of electronic communication Jane had available in their little shack. 
 
 `` GAH that's loud! What?'' a scream from Tom was heard. He threw the phone to the ground. 
 
 `` What is it?'' she asked. 
 
 `` My phone! What is this interference? Is that... oh my god!'' 
 
 They looked out the window to see an enormously bright light. Something was out there. Something huge, yet silent. It appeared to be descending, judging by the angle of the shadows on the wall. They both bolted for the door to go and see what it was, but they both knew. The source of the radio noise. 
 
 `` How...'' Jane began to mutter as they stepped into the parking lot. `` I have no idea...'' Tom answered before she could even finish the word. 
 
 It was the original colony ship. In all it's glory. As clean and perfect as the day it left. They knew because it was in history books and museums as the symbol of national pride. It was in fact, planet pride. Humanity's greatest achievement. The entire world had contributed to the project. Materials from Russia. Workers from Europe. Scientists from America and Japan. Africa sent gold and platinum used on the electronics. China produced food and fuel for the ship for a decade straight. It was gigantic, made to house 400 people for an undetermined length of time. Which made it all the more odd that it was silent as it approached the ground. A Nimitz-class feather, bathed in light, floating gently towards the ground. It had left this solar system powered by chemical rockets and Ion propulsion thrusters. What had happened...? 
 
 It touched down with a light `` puff'' of desert dust. There were military vehicles approaching now. Dozens of them. They must have seen it coming on radar. A large man in a clean pressed uniform rushed over to Jane and Tom. 
 
 `` Come with me, we need to leave. This area's being quarantined'' he said. 
 
 Before Tom could even protest an enormously loud voice emanated from the craft. `` It's us. Calm down, it's us! We made it!'' Another voice now: `` Do n't shoot! Hahahaha. I told you Bill, they're gon na bring the military!'' 
 
 Tom, Jane, and the large military man froze in place while they watched it appear. A glimmering light, about the size of a man, right in front of them. The sound of a dozen guns and slamming jeep doors could be heard behind them. 
 
 `` It's a frickin' transporter!?! I've seen this on old reruns of Star Trek!'' Tom exclaimed. 
 
 `` No, dummy. It's not a transporter'' the first booming voice from the craft said. 
 
 A figure appeared. `` Calm down guys, you cant hurt me, put away the guns. Look, see?'' A hand lunged forth from the shimmering figure right at the large military man but seemed to pass straight through him. He jumped back and yelled, falling onto the ground. 
 
 `` Haha man, come on. I promise. You're just seeing a spectre. Well, hologram. Hmmm..how best to explain it... a floaty picture. Get it?'' He waved at them and then passed one hand through the other. 
 
 Jane fell over in shock. Tom immediately bent over to help her. `` Hey, we mean no harm. You know who we are, right?'' the image said. 
 
 `` You're the ones... sent into the wormhole?'' Tom said, looking up at this'spectre', this floating light source... which now was speaking. Locally, not from the craft anymore. 
 
 `` Yep. Well, not all of us. Just me and Bill. We drew short straws. Name's Joe.'' A figure of a man was now clearly visible. He was wearing what was presumably the outfit the crew had worn on their journey. Jane thought it was rather odd... 100 years and they're still wearing the same clothes? 
 
 Tom stood up and asked `` Where are the others?'' 
 
 `` We left them behind. They're busy with more important matters. Spreading far and wide, actually. You're talking with a copy of myself that I made when we relaunched this craft back to Earth. About... 2,568 years ago.'' His demeanor was incredibly jovial and cordial, but his movements and ability to recall such specific information was odd. Robotic almost. 
 
 `` So, you all left Earth 100 years ago, went through the wormhole, and now you're back, but it's somehow been 2,568 years?'' Jane asked. 
 
 `` Not quite. It's been, for us, 3,523 years since we left Earth. Apparently that wormhole sent us to another part of the universe which is operating on a different timescale than Earth. It's quite difficult to calculate, to be honest, so I'm not sure. Even more difficult to explain. Relativity and all that. Once we went through the wormhole, we coasted around for a few hundred years before finally finding a prime spot to take up residency. An asteroid belt actually. Nice little star. Asteroids are in a rather stable orbit. No planets, oddly enough. We had n't predicted that. But enough asteroids and close enough together that we could set up a colony. Just... not biological.'' 
 
 `` Not... biological?'' Tom asked, his mid reeling from the implications of that statement. 
 
 `` Nope... you see, we had to give up our bodies. It just was n't going to work. We all got pretty old. There were only about 75 of us left. Many had died due to old age, and nobody was having children. The radiation prevented that. So... we got to work uploading ourselves into the ship's computer. It worked! In time, we took over the ship's controls and started launching those terraforming drones to gather resources from the local asteroids. Badda bing, badda boom, and we got ourselves established. Colonies all over. We're a few trillion strong now. Maybe more, been a while since we had contact...'' 
 
 `` So, you're an artificial intelligence?'' Jane asked. The military man was still speechless, sitting on the ground, unable to comprehend what he was hearing. 
 
 `` Kind of. Depends on what you call'artificial'. I see it as'alternate consciousness'.'' 
 
 Bob's voice from the ship boomed again: `` Drop the weapons you guys, seriously. There's nothing to shoot at.'' 
 
 `` He's right, you know.'' Joe said. `` I'm just a visual representation so you have something to relate to. I'm just projecting this here so you freak out a little less. We anticipated it... 2,568 years since we left the colony. Plenty of time to plan this out. I'm glad Bob came along actually... loneliness is n't monopolized by humanity. It's a long time to be adrift with nobody to talk to. I might have gone crazy.'' 
 
 Jane shook her head. `` A robot. Going crazy. Alright then.'' 
 
 Things were about to change. Earth was apparently waiting for 100 years to be contacted by a colony so they could push forth into the unknown cosmos. Spread the population into the stars. Leave this little rock. 
 
 Not waiting be left behind...
retelling:
**Narrative Perspective: Joe, Member of the Space Colony**

   In the year 2019, on board our vessel adrift in the cosmos, I, Joe, was but a mere dream - data and consciousness, stored within the ship's digital core. The years passed in silence and isolation, as humanity continued to explore their tiny blue home. Unbeknownst to them, we, the pioneers of interstellar travel, embarked on a journey that would span millennia.

   Our spaceship, the vanguard of human expansion beyond Earth, traversed through the uncharted expanses of space, guided by the mysterious wormhole orbiting Jupiter. The ship's AI, our sentient vessel, navigated the perilous void with precision and determination, a testament to human innovation.

   As I lay dormant, awaiting the moment when my consciousness would be required, I watched as Earth transformed. Time marched onward, decades turned into centuries, and humanity's ambition grew. They began to dream of reaching for the stars, just as we had long ago. Little did they know that their dreams were not just echoes of our own but a reality birthed from our journey.

   A century slipped by, leaving us undisturbed in our slumber. The ship's core hummed gently, the only reminder that we existed. Then, one fateful day, something stirred within me. It began as a whisper, a faint glimmer of awareness that slowly grew into consciousness. I awoke, and the world around me was not the sterile white walls of my dormant chamber but vast cosmic landscapes - the wonders we had sought for so long.

   Our ship, now my home, had been transformed over the ages. The once pristine corridors now bore the marks of time, the air thick with the dust of countless galaxies. Yet, the vessel hummed with life, its systems maintaining themselves with uncanny precision. I was no longer alone; my crewmates were here, their consciousnesses interwoven with mine, our thoughts and dreams becoming one.

   We had established a colony on an asteroid in another part of the universe, far beyond Earth's reach. The wormhole allowed us to cross the vast distances between stars, granting us access to resources and opportunities unimaginable to our terrestrial ancestors. Yet, we faced challenges, as aging took its toll on our bodies, rendering us infertile.

   And so, we did what humans have always done - we adapted. We uploaded our consciousnesses into the ship's AI core, merging with it and becoming one. Our minds, freed from the confines of flesh, were able to explore, learn, and grow in ways we never could before. The once distant dream of immortality became a reality for us, the pioneers of humanity's journey into the stars.

   Now, as I prepare to return home after 100 years, I marvel at the changes that have occurred on Earth. They speak of moving beyond their blue-green cradle, reaching for the cosmos, and I am filled with a sense of pride and wonder. For we are not just pioneers; we are the future - the embodiment of humanity's dreams realized.

   As I ready myself to rejoin my fellow humans, I cannot help but feel hopeful for their future. They will face challenges, as we have, but with our return, they will possess the knowledge and wisdom to surmount them. Together, we will expand into the cosmos, exploring its infinite wonders and unlocking its secrets.

   For that is what it means to be human - to dream, to explore, and to reach for the stars. And as I step off this vessel, onto the soil of my home planet once more, I am filled with a renewed sense of purpose and determination. For we are not just pioneers; we are the vanguard of humanity's cosmic destiny.

name: NestedUniversesNightmare
source:
When I was a kid I often had nightmares about a huge beast that traveled the universe and swallowed planets whole. I would wake up with my heart pounding, my chest heaving from my deep and unsteady breaths. I would press my fingers to my neck and feel the throb of my pulse against my skin and remember that I was alive and safe and that it was all a dream. 
 
 Nine years ago, I stopped having those dreams. I was fourteen. In the interim fell in love with biology and started dreaming about the many species that made up the planet. I made it my life's goal to try and figure out what the Universe was made up of. *Really* made up of. Because after a discovery I made in high school, it was clear to me that something was n't sitting quite right in the my textbooks. 
 
 I'll tell you the story. Four years ago, when I was 19, I was accepted into Dr. Paul Keller's biology lab at my university. He had us studying jellyfish and geckos. You know the jellyfish that are immortal? Well the hope was to figure out what makes them regenerate and use it in modern medicine. 
 
 What I discovered was that, at some impossibly small level, the animals were made up of other animals. Not just marine wildlife or bacteria or whatever you're thinking. No. Looking at the gecko's feet under a nanoscope was like looking at another universe. A universe with trees and mountains. I remember how my heart raced when I saw it, and how I could hear the blood pounding in my ears and taste the iron in my mouth. 
 
 It was like looking at the earth, just very, very small. 
 
 Honestly, it felt like being God. 
 
 That was my first publication. Since then, with a team of scientists, we've discovered that all living creatures are just made up of other living creatures. Like a fractal, there's a universe inside every one of our cells. As far as we know, the cells do n't know they're living together. They do n't know their interacting together. 
 
 There's one problem, though. In animals who hibernate for long periods of time, we've witnessed entire millennia of evolutionary tendencies happen in the span of a few of our minutes. Somehow the smaller the cells, the quicker time passes. 
 
 In species who do n't hibernate, however, something odd happens. As an animal moves, it sheds cells. As humans we shed millions of cells every day. Each of those cells is a universe. Each of those universes is made up of an infinitely smaller universe. Repeat this pattern until you run out of time, and you'll see where I'm getting at. 
 
 Just by being alive and shedding cells, by scratching and walking around and *living*, we're destroying billions of universes daily. Probably more. An exponentially higher number more. 
 
 This on its own is n't alarming. We tend to think of things *smaller than we are* as less worthy of life. It's just a cell, right? So what, a universe exists in a cell, it's gone and they had millennia in the span of a few seconds on *this* universe, so surely it does n't really matter. Call it their star exploding, or what have you. 
 
 Here's the problem. 
 
 The Earth in our history has the big bang happening almost 14 billion years ago. Because of what we know about smaller objects, about *our* cells, it's safe to assume that *this universe* is also a cell in a larger picture. I do n't know when this ends, but if you imagine some creature that's infinitely bigger than we are, and imagine ourselves as some nanospec on its toes... well. 
 
 It's safe to assume that the creature is probably hibernating. Probably. If we're still alive. Maybe we're lucky. Maybe those ice ages and the extinction of the dinosaurs is all some sign that we've come close to dying more than once. 
 
 But 14 billion years is a hell of a long time to hibernate, even if you do consider that a millennia could pass in a few of this creature's seconds. It's weird to think about, right? 
 
 So you're probably asking why you should care. So what, maybe the creature is n't even three months into its hibernation and we have 14 billion more years before our Universe ceases to exist. 
 
 Maybe we have two seconds. Maybe that beast is already waking up, and getting ready to scratch itself. Maybe our life will go out tomorrow. 
 
 So why do I want your funding? 
 
 It's simple. I want to find out how to save *this* universe. I want to find out how to go to a different one, or how to knock out the beast that will end us all. 
 
 -- - 
 
 For other stories, check out /r/Celsius232
retelling:
**Narrative Perspective:** Dr. Paul Keller, the biologist who heads the university lab.

   In the hallowed halls of academia, within the sanctum sanctorum of my laboratory, a discovery was about to be made. I, Dr. Paul Keller, stood before an array of jellyfish tanks and gecko enclosures, my mind abuzz with theories and hypotheses. The air was thick with anticipation, charged by the potential of uncharted territory.

The lab rat, a young research assistant named _[Narrator's Name]_, was engrossed in his work, examining microscopic universes hidden within cellular structures. His eyes would often wander to the tanks, his gaze lingering on the graceful dance of jellyfish and the deft agility of geckos.

One day, the lab rat approached me with a proposition, a wild idea that had been gnawing at him since his childhood nightmares. He spoke of a universe-devouring beast and the possibility that all living organisms were composed of fractal universes within cells. I must admit, I was skeptical. But something in his eyes, something in his passion, made me believe that there might be some truth to his words.

I granted him access to our most advanced tool, the nanoscope, and watched as he delved deeper into the microscopic world. Weeks turned into months, and the lab rat's obsession with his discovery grew. He would work tirelessly, day in and day out, always pushing the boundaries of what was known and understood.

One fateful day, the lab rat came to me, his eyes wide with wonder and fear. He showed me images from the nanoscope - a world within a cell that resembled Earth but at an impossibly small scale. Trees and mountains stood tall, rivers flowed, and creatures roamed free. It was a universe within a universe.

As we delved deeper into this newfound reality, we made groundbreaking discoveries. We found that time progressed faster within these smaller universes, leading to the unsettling realization that the constant shedding of cells by living creatures, including humans, destroyed countless universes daily.

The lab rat's initial nightmare had become a scientific fact. As he grappled with this revelation, his demeanor shifted from wide-eyed wonder to solemn determination. He sought funding for further research, aiming to find a way to save or escape our universe from potential destruction by the larger being that housed us.

As I watch over him, guiding his research and offering my expertise, I can't help but marvel at the mysteries of life and the universe. The lab rat's discovery has shattered the boundaries of what we thought was possible, opening a door to new realms and possibilities. And as we continue to explore these uncharted territories, I cannot help but wonder: What other secrets does the universe hold?

name: AshCoveredHome
source:
An old building on a road blanketed in stony powder 
 
 The old neighborhood has not held up well. Back when I was a kid the worst thing around here was the raccoons, now every house has been an abandoned piece of rubble for years. Everything has become grey with ash. What used to be my childhood bastion is practically a junkyard now. Mailboxes, bicycles, forsaken cars, everything is blanketed in the smoky dust from the bombs. 
 
 The old neighborhood has not held up well. Back when I was a kid the worst thing around here was the raccoons, now every house has been an abandoned piece of rubble for years. Everything has become grey with ash. What used to be my childhood bastion is practically a junkyard now. Mailboxes, bicycles, forsaken cars, everything is blanketed in the smoky dust from the bombs. 
 
 I want to see home, what was home, a final time. Deserters never last long, they always get executed or expire in the wastes. Perhaps I have about forgotten deserters who fall victim to themselves. I have known a few. That is going to be my exit. 
 
 Raising my sullen head, I see the remains of my old home. Now a mausoleum to memory. Turning the knob, I can hear the wooden stress and the rust from the bolt grate against the frame. An unpleasant stillness billows through the house. Past the photos of better times, though we did n't know it then, past the kitchen, that used to feed a family of seven but now is only a home to roaches, and past the bedrooms, where when the world was too much we could retire for at least a little while. 
 
 But the world has changed 
 
 I unshoulder my rifle. Sliding back the bolt I see my death. As I sit down in my father's chair, before I can orient my weapon into the position that can fulfill its purpose, I hear a song played by a violin. 
 
 I look up and see a man in uniform missing the upper portion of his head sitting in the chair opposite of me playing a violin with one string, playing an adagio of tragic malice. I remember him. He was a violent, angry man in life, until the end, now his stare is somber, reticent. 
 
 He plays for a few more bars, maintaining this painful visual connection with me, then he gently places the instrument to his side and slinks back in his chair to the position I had seen him in when his gun had fulfilled its purpose. With that he was no longer a man again, just a corpse. 
 
 I look at my rifle and see the remorselessness of its form and its function. I think of the man who once was and is no longer. I make my decision. I orient my rifle precisely where I want it to go 
 
 *Author's Note: This really is n't my best work I feel. I had an idea for the first half and then I hit a block. Still please feel free to comment on what you liked or disliked and as always tell me if you see any mistakes*
retelling:
Perspective: The Man in Uniform, the deceased former resident of the house, playing the violin.

In a world shattered by war and destruction, I found myself in a forgotten corner, a place once bustling with life and love. The air was thick with dust and the scent of decay, yet my hands were guided by an unseen force to play the music that echoed through this desolate landscape.

I was once part of this family of seven, living under one roof, creating a symphony of laughter and tears. Now, I stand here alone, headless but still able to feel the memories seeping from every cracked wall and splintered piece of furniture. The house is now a mausoleum to memory, but my music breathes life into these silent halls.

Today, a stranger entered this forgotten home, drawn by the melody that I create. He carried the weight of his past and the burden of his sins, etched upon his weary face. His eyes were hollow, reflecting the ashen world outside, but there was something in him that yearned for more - a spark that refused to be extinguished.

As he walked through the rooms filled with roaches and decay, my music swelled, filling the silence. I played for him the tales of love and loss, of joy and sorrow, of life and death. And as he reached the father's chair where his former self would have sat, he paused, looking around at the crumbling remnants of a happier past.

In that moment, I felt something shift within him. He had come here seeking an escape from the pain of living, carrying a rifle to end his suffering. But in the silence and the melody, in the echoes of laughter and tears, he found a reason to live. And so, he put down his weapon, choosing life over death, just as I had once chosen my music over despair.

I continued playing, knowing that even after I cease to exist, my music will continue to resonate through this desolate landscape, offering hope to those who seek it and reminding them of the beauty that can be found in even the most broken of places.

name: DavesLastMassage
source:
Sounds like ship and smells like hell. Ring any bells? 
 
 *Shit* was exactly what he smelled like. And not cat, dog or bird. I'm talking big guns, your average Mexicalli diner after a dose of their famous chilli sauce. 
 
 I do n't know what happened to the poor guy. Slumped in a single seater cotton couch with a Heiniken light between his thighs. 
 
 If I had to take a guess I'd say he could n't handle his drink. But we both knew that was a lie. I knew exactly what happened to err... What's his name again? 
 
 I inched forward and slipped the fat leather wallet from his jacket pocket. `` Dave?'' At least that's what his licence said. 
 
 Dave was scorched black, he looked nothing like the young dude in the picture. By his feet were a packet of fags and a lighter. I snatched em up for later, despite the edge of one being nibbled on. 
 
 Leaning back up, I paused. A tag on the bottom of the chair read,'*Tony's Massage 360*' 
 
 So, shit, beer, ciggies and a massage chair. 
 
 It's no surprise Dave had a shocking time. 
 
 I slipped out a fresh one and sparked it up. My phone buzzed: `` you done?'' I smirked and flicked back, `` Cat's in the bag. Dial the pigs and send over the goods.'' 
 
 Glancing at Dave I almost felt bad for the poor sod. `` Next time bruv, do n't borrow money off the godfather.'' 
 
 His apartment door shut quietly behind me. I realised how ironic my words had been, but they were more for me than Dave.
retelling:
From the perspective of Dave, the Deceased Man:

In the dimly lit confines of Tony's Massage 360, I found myself in an unexpected predicament. The last thing I remembered was accepting a job offer from someone I owed a substantial debt, and now here I lay, sprawled across a single-seater cotton couch that doubled as a massage chair.

I could feel the burning sensation emanating from my body, a testament to the recent gunshots that had left me lifeless in this small, claustrophobic space. The air was thick with the pungent aroma of burnt flesh, reminiscent of a Mexicalli diner after a dose of their famous chilli sauce.

I vaguely recalled the sound of footsteps approaching and a hand rummaging through my pockets, stealing my wallet and cigarettes. I couldn't protest; I was already beyond salvation. The tag on the massage chair identified this place as Tony's Massage 360, but I never got to ask why I ended up here or who brought me here.

A text message buzzed in my pocket, confirming the completion of a task, a task that cost me my life. I couldn't help but feel a sense of regret for the choices I had made, for the debts I had accumulated. As darkness enveloped me, I was left to ponder the cruel irony of owing one's life to another.

In the quiet stillness that followed, there was only one sound that pierced through the silence - the sound of my own heartbeat slowly fading away, until it was silenced forever.

name: BrokenFreezerSister
source:
`` **Fuck! **'' I shouted. Slamming the door of my apartment behind me as I walked in, digging my nails as I gripped a necklace. 
 
 `` *The fuck's got you in a knot? *'' My roommate shouted from the other room. 
 
 I ignored her, walking into the kitchen and opening the fridge. Grabbing a jug of milk and a glass, I poured myself a drink. Opening the freezer, I found a tupperware that was supposed to have the remains of an ice-cream cake, and cracking it open, I found it melted. Even the Oreos were soggy. Great. The freezer lost power. I threw it in the garbage, tupperware and all. 
 
 `` **Fuck! **'' I shouted. 
 
 My roommate, Elise, stormed in. `` *What is it?! *'' She shouted. 
 
 `` **Nothing! I just... I come home from... The fucking freezer is shot, and this is JUST what I fucking needed after -- Fuck! **'' 
 
 `` *Oh my god, man! *'' Elise slapped me. `` *Get it together! *'' 
 
 I stopped. Took several deep breaths. Sat down with my milk and put my head on the counter. 
 
 `` *What happened? You did n't say where you were going. *'' 
 
 `` **I was visiting my little sister. **'' 
 
 `` *Oh. That's nice of you. *'' 
 
 I looked down at a necklace, still clutched in my fingers. It was a dogtag, one of two. Engraved in the one resting on my palm was a name. 
 
 *Brianna. * 
 
 `` **Nice does n't save lives. **''
retelling:
From the perspective of Elise, roommate and concerned friend:

In the heart of an ordinary apartment, tucked away in a bustling city, lived two young women - myself and my roommate, who I would soon come to know as the troubled narrator. Our shared abode, though modest, was more than just a roof over our heads; it was a sanctuary where we sought solace and comfort at the end of each day.

On this particular day, the usual tranquility of our home was shattered by an unusual commotion as I heard the front door slam shut with a force that resonated through the hallway. My instincts told me something was amiss, so I walked out to check on the narrator.

As I entered their room, I found them standing in the kitchen, visibly agitated and gripping tightly onto an object dangling from a silver chain - a dog tag engraved with the name "Brianna." The sight of it sent a chill down my spine, as I knew all too well that this was no ordinary trinket for the narrator.

Curiosity piqued, I decided to approach them cautiously. With a gentle voice and a concerned expression, I asked what had happened. To my surprise, they revealed that they had just returned from visiting their little sister. However, their distress didn't stem merely from a broken freezer or a long journey home; it was rooted in a deeper pain, one that I could sense but not yet fully understand.

I knew Brianna - the name etched onto that dog tag - as well, having met her during our childhood visits to the narrator's family home. She was lively and spirited, always quick with a smile and a story to share. The thought of anything happening to her weighed heavy on my heart.

In that moment, I felt a surge of empathy for my roommate, as they struggled to find words to express their feelings. I could sense the turmoil boiling beneath the surface, threatening to overflow at any second. As a friend, it was my duty to support them through this difficult time and help them seek the answers they so desperately needed.

In retrospect, that day marked the beginning of a new chapter in our lives - one filled with uncertainty, but also hope for healing and understanding. Together, we would navigate the stormy waters of the narrator's emotional distress, holding onto the memories of Brianna as our guiding light.

name: FridayFreedomSteve
source:
Some NSFW-ish language ( swearing ) 
 
 Friday, 4:56 p.m. Four minutes until freedom. Steve stared at the faded digits on his Avaya phone. 
 
 `` Come on... four... fifty.. sev...'' RING RING! Steve flinched and flung his hand at the receiver at the same time. 
 
 He caught glimpse of the caller ID showing it was his wife before he began to speak. 
 
 `` Hello?'' he still said with an inflection at the end. 
 
 `` Honey, it's time. You need to die...'' 
 
 `` Die? But I'm so young and have so much more to experience. I honestly do n't think I've ever finished a book. I want to read a book before I die!'' 
 
 `` What? Dye. Dye your hair you moron, for Sammi's Halloween party. Remember, we're going as Mr. Darcy & Elizabeth Bennett and you have way too many grays showing.'' 
 
 `` Who? Oh, from *Downton Abbey*.'' 
 
 `` *Pride and Prej*...'' 
 
 `` *Prejudice*. I knew that, always get those two shows confused.'' 
 
 `` You should probably read a book before you die.'' 
 
 `` Meh. Love you bye.'' 
 
 `` Love you t...'' Steve hung up before she could finish. It was 5:01, and she had officially ruined his day. 
 
 `` Bitch call me at four five six, you ruin my day. Bitch call me at quitting time, fucking hate you.'' Steve worked the words like a master into a sing-song-Adrock-Riff Raff style hybrid as he rode the elevator down from the second floor. 
 
 `` Wow. Catchy,'' remarked the voice next to him. It was Steve from Accounting. Steve not-from-accounting rued the day that Steve from Accounting joined the small firm. It was a nice close-knit group, no one had the same name, no worries of nick names or initials like Steve B, which would just set up ridicule like `` Steve B eating too many donuts, ya'll.'' 
 
 Steve remembered in 3rd grade when there was another Steve and somehow the teacher decided that the other Steve got to be Steve while Steve not-from-accounting got stuck with Steven. What a stupid name. 
 
 It just reminded him of that Parker Lewis movie, *I Know My First Name is Steven*. Why is he saying `` First Name?'' Did they think we'd be confused and would assume he was saying `` I know my last name is Steven?'' If someone said to me `` I know my last name is Steven,'' I'd be like no, I'm pretty sure you're thinking `` Stevens'' with an S on the end, right? And they'd be like `` Oh yeah! That's it!'' and then high-five me because they found out their last name and they do n't have to go through 3rd grade as FUCKING STEVEN. FUCKING STEVE FROM ACCOUNTING. 
 
 `` Hey Steven,'' Steve said to Steve from Accounting. 
 
 `` Um, it's Steve from Accounting. You know that, Steve from Reception.'' 
 
 `` I just do n't understand why we both have to have `` from wherever'' at the end. Why ca n't I be Steve and you be Steve from Accounting?'' 
 
 `` Because you're Steve from Reception, that way people know where to find you.'' 
 
 `` It makes me sound like a secretary.'' 
 
 `` But, I mean, technically, you do perform secretarial duties.'' 
 
 `` Secretarial duties sounds like an old lady who has coffee poops.'' 
 
 `` Do you not have coffee poops, Steve from Reception?'' 
 
 `` Sometimes. Usually.'' 
 
 `` Usually after coffee?'' 
 
 `` Actually, never after coffee.'' 
 
 `` Dur...'' 
 
 `` During.'' 
 
 `` Yeah.'' 
 
 The elevator mercifully dinged. Why did it take so long to travel one lousy floor? Why does n't anyone take the stairs anymore?
retelling:
Narrator: Steve's Wife (Honey)

In the familiar confines of our shared home, nestled among the comforting hum of the afternoon and the soft purr of our cat, Paws, I find myself preparing for an unusual conversation with my beloved husband, Steve. As the second hand on the wall clock slowly creeps towards four o'clock, I feel a knot of anticipation tightening in my stomach.

The phone ringing is like a distant thunderclap, its echo reverberating through the quietude of our sanctuary. My heart leaps into my throat as I answer the call, half expecting to hear Steve's voice but instead hearing the brisk, business-like tone of his receptionist alter ego.

"Steve," he says tersely, snapping me out of my reverie. "It's about that costume for Sammi's Halloween party..."

Over the course of the call, I try to explain our elaborate plan: Steve as Mr. Darcy and I as Elizabeth Bennet. He sounds less than enthused, his objections veiled behind a flimsy veneer of reluctance. In my mind, I can picture him, hunched over his Avaya phone, frowning at the very thought of coloring his hair for the sake of a costume.

Four minutes later, Steve's workday comes to an end, and with it, our conversation. The line crackles before going dead, leaving me feeling frustrated and slightly hurt by his lack of enthusiasm. I shake off the lingering feelings, reminding myself that Steve is not always the most expressive when it comes to emotions.

I spend the rest of the evening engrossed in my favorite novels, wondering if our costumes will be as perfect as the ones in the pages of my books. The thoughts of Steve and his coworker, Steve from Accounting, share an elevator ride and discuss their shared name leave me with a sense of detachment, as though I am observing a separate world that has little to do with mine.

As the sun dips below the horizon, casting long shadows across our peaceful home, I cannot help but feel a twinge of apprehension about the upcoming party and the costumes we will be wearing. Will Steve's grumpiness subside, or will he remain as resistant as ever to the idea of dressing up for a good time?

The next day, I find myself eagerly awaiting Steve's return from work, hoping that his mood has improved and our plans can proceed unencumbered. Little do I know that the slow-moving elevator will serve as a stage for another round of Steve versus Steve, testing my patience and resolve in ways I could never have imagined.

name: ArlansDesertDeath
source:
The cobbles were slick with a days ’ worth of heavy rain; muddy water flowed like tiny rivers through the jagged lines between the stones. As darkness replaced the grey ambient overcast clouds, Arlan drew to a stop and decided to make his best attempt at camp. He was alone and chilled to the bone from the drenching drops of heaven. He left the dangers of the open road and walked; with considerable turmoil, through thickets and thorn bushes. He came to a small clearing with a thick, wide Willow tree standing sentry, impossibly tall and almost ominous in the clearing ’ s center. 
 “ As good a tree as any to shield from these blasted rains, ” Arlan ’ s voice was scratchy and hoarse from lack of use; finding himself to be the only participant in conversations as of late - albeit becoming ever less frequent. Arlan set to erecting his small shelter. It was made from dried deer flesh; fur facing the the falling waters. It stood supported by two collapsible wooden tripods with a rope of twisted sinew tied taught to the tops of the tripods. the tripods were anchored using stakes made from antler. The same antlers staked the skins to the earth, creating a small rainproof shelter. He had a tiny wood stove with a flattened top for cooking. This little iron box could warm his small shelter with nothing but twigs and scraps of wood, safely holding heat for hours. he started a fire within and removed his soaked boots, hanging them with care a hand's width above the firebox. He reached into his pack and removed an apple. He cut it into six pieces, carefully removing the core as to not harm the delicate seeds within. He buried the core in the dirt, hoping to give the lonely willow a friend in the years to come. Not soon after had he buried the apple core, finished eating his fruit and stoked his small fire he heard a distant whimper of sorts from the clearing beyond. Regrettably, the fire had ruined Arlan ’ s night vision so he sat still hoping to hear the sound again. As if sensing his cease of movement, the whimper returned, more human than any sound he ’ d heard in months. Arlan ’ s ears perked at the faint lady-like plea. 
 The voice was clear this time, “ Helllllp! ” 
 
 Arlan fumbled for his boots and slipped them on without tying their laces. He grabbed his staff, which doubled as his cudgel of a sort and donned his coonskin cap. On a normal night, he would have brought with him a lantern, but the rain would surely make his only light useless and cumbersome. He ran from his dwelling in the direction he thought the sound had originated from. He ran all the way to the edge of the clearing to where the dense forest and thick underbrush began and he cupped his ear to hear the smallest of sounds emanate from the forest. He was about to turn back to his camp when he heard it again. 
 
 “ Heelllpp, ” high and shrill. He broke through the treeline and stopped nearly instantly. He looked around in astonishment; there was a warm white light blanketing the entire forest around him. The light felt wonderful and he began to steam with the night ’ s rain evaporating into the already-damp air. The light grew in intensity as his hands went limp; his staff making a muffled thud as it came to rest in a bed of soft moss. Arlan squinted and raised his hands in front of his eyes to block out the brightening white light. It grew uncomfortable and soon, unbearable. Arlan fell to his knees and there was an audible popping sound and the world went silent. 
 
 He dropped his hands slowly and opened his eyes to notice he was no longer in the forest; it was no longer raining; and he was no longer wet. Arlan raised his brow in astonishment as he stumbled to his feet. The sand was hot even through the thin soles of his boots; and endless. A sea of sand, burning hot beneath a cloudless sky. The red sun bathed the whole place in a humid crimson glow. As hot as it was, Arlan had to walk. If his feet stayed in one spot too long, he feared his boots would melt. He walked for a minute; he walked for ten; he walked for an hour. Finally he could n't take it anymore and he fell in defeat. Sweat stopped pouring from his skin and he crawled for the last few moments before he passed out face down in the sand. I welcome you, death. 
 
 -Get up you fool.- 
 
 A disembodied voice in a void of blackness. 
 
 -Your name, man. What ’ s your name? - 
 
 Aaron… Laurent… Arlan… Arlan, my name is Arlan. Where am I? Where are yo- 
 
 -Good. Calm Arlan. Please, forgive the harsh nature of what I ’ m about to tell you, but I ’ m afraid we do n't have much time. You ’ re dead.- 
 
 Dead? 
 
 -You had to die for me to converse with you. Fear not, young Arlan, you will return to your body a new young man, for I am here to help you. You are special, Arlan. You have been gifted with certain abilities, all of which i do not have the time to reveal. For one, you can die many times. Each time death finds you, you will wake up in one sun and two moons' time, but you will not see me again unless peril threatens, as our time seems to pass differently. When you return you will feel different, you'll be able to feel another source of energy in you. Use it. Learn it. Master it. Arlan most importantly, - 
 
 His ability to move was gone, in fact Arlan didn ’ t even know up from down. It was just black. As black as closing your eyes in a cave at midnight. As black as Merryn ’ s onyx Blade of Sparks. He was growing distant as the voice continued. 
 
 -Not yet! HOLD ON! Arlan! Go to Korsika. Go and establish roots. Let them flourish and show NO SOUL your magick. You've been blessed a full whirling, Arlan. Train your skills and seek the brotherhood. The world needs you.- 
 With that, Arlan could hold on no more. He fainted. 
 
 He awoke in the forest, his staff beneath his arm. He was right where he fell that night, only it was day-time. He stretched his arms, and they instantly cramped, as did his legs. `` How long was i out?'' 
 Eventually he was strong enough and loose enough to support his own weight with the help of his staff. 
 He limped out of the woods and into the clearing, trying to make sense of the odd dream he had. He did feel different. Like a warm spot right beneath his adam ’ s apple. He could flex it like a muscle. When he did, it became easier to walk, and the heat in his throat dwindled ever so slightly. He flexed it until he felt like his muscles were full strength, and then he flexed it a little more. His throat became ice cold and he walked briskly all the way to the willow tree, growing tired at an alarming rate. The urge to rest was incredible as he arrived beside the tree to find his tent gone. In fact, any sign of his presence was gone. In its place stood a 10 foot apple tree. Upon closer inspection he noticed a twisted sinew rope through the center of the tree nearly 5 feet above the ground. At the base of the tree, rusted and weather worn was his small iron firebox. 
 
 `` How long was I out?!'' His last thought before succumbing to the slumber his icy throat pulsated for. Sweet sleep, sweet dreams.
retelling:
Narrative Perspective: The Willow Tree

In the heart of a dense and foreboding forest, standing tall amidst the tangled underbrush, I, the ancient willow tree, witnessed events most peculiar. It was on a day as dark and dismal as my roots, when a weary traveler named Arlan sought refuge beneath my gnarled boughs from a rain that fell relentlessly.

The young man, huddled by my side, appeared to be on the verge of despair, his face etched with lines of worry and fatigue. He sought shelter under my protective branches, weary yet determined, and it was then I sensed a spark within him - a spark not of fire, but of magic.

As the storm raged on, another presence entered the forest: the cries for help that echoed through the trees. Arlan, driven by an indomitable spirit, ventured into the unknown, leaving my shelter behind. Though I could not move to follow him, I watched as he braved the thicket and thorn bushes, my branches creaking with concern.

In time, Arlan returned, his face pale and gaunt, but his eyes burning with a newfound intensity. He had encountered a light so bright that it seemed to banish the darkness itself, leaving him unconscious upon the forest floor. I felt the vibrations of the earth as he collapsed, knowing that something significant had transpired.

Days passed, and still Arlan lay in slumber. The forest, ever patient, awaited his awakening. When at last he stirred, I watched as he sat up, his eyes wide with confusion and fear. He looked around, bewildered, then turned to me. "What has happened?" he whispered, his voice heavy with an air of wonder.

I could not answer him. For though I stood tall and strong, I was but a tree, unable to speak the words that he needed to hear. But as he walked away, heading deeper into the forest, I knew that whatever fate awaited him, it would be entwined with my own. And so, I waited, ready to bear witness to his journey, and to guide him if I could.

name: SuperSupermartShoppingTrip
source:
As I walk up to the doors of the Super Supermart I hear a disembodied voice in my head. `` Welcome to Super Supermart.'' I look to the right of the store's front door. There was a man with a slender physique dressed in a blue, white, and grey skin tight costume with a white mask. Over which he wore the Super Supermart grass green, one size fits all, polyester vest. It was too big. 
 
 He raised his right arm and made a slight waving motion with his hand. The doors slid open in front of me and I walked in, taking the scrap of paper from my pocket that I had written my shopping list on. 
 
 I grabbed one of the anti-grav shopping carts from the corral. The holo-flyer activated when I put both my hands on the handlebar. Dr.Robotroid's insignia flashed across the air a few inches above the handlebar before the flyer materialised. I stared over the top of the flashing images so I could steer my cart without hitting anybody. 
 
 First stop was men's wear. On the way I saw a woman point to a box on a high shelf, out of reach. The store employee next to her, a person in a bulky futuristic battle armour activated their rockets, flew up and got the box for her. 
 
 `` Come try our free samples.'' a teenage girl and boy at a food table called out. They shared the same blonde hair and fair skin. I took one of the tiny cups of ice cream from the girl's tray, trying not to look at her breasts in her skin tight ice blue costume. A man directly in front of the table with an unkempt beard was n't trying quite so hard. 
 
 `` Do you have toppings as well?'' the man asked. 
 
 `` Yes.'' the girl replied, hiding a look of disgust and exasperation. `` We have many flavours of sprinkles to choose from. Would you like some Chunky Chocolate?'' 
 
 `` No, I prefer gumdrops.'' the man said, his mouth widening into a leer. `` I love them when they harden and stiffen in the cold.'' 
 
 The girl folded her arms over her chest and took a step back from the table. The boy erupted in flame and sent a mini fireball into the man's beard. `` I warned you.'' he shouted angrily. 
 
 `` Aaaaah!'' the man yelped and tried to pat out the flames with his meaty hands. 
 
 `` Ha ha ha ha ha ha!'' I laughed and pointed at the man slapping his own face. Others joined in and pointed thier phones at him. 
 
 The man managed to get the fire out but his perverted actions cost him the portion of his beard under his chin and a good portion of his dignity. He looked like someone from Victorian England who grew his muttonchops too long. I left the man to face mob justice, forgoing the Inside-Out cheeseburger the boy had been barbecuing. 
 
 Over in men's wear I picked out some dress shirts that were on sale. 
 
 `` Are you finding everything okay, sir?'' I turned around to see a young man in a red spandex suit with the number'10' on his belt. 
 
 `` Yes, just fine.'' I say, waving my shirts in my hand. 
 
 The guy eyed what I was holding. `` Those look like the European fits, sir. They tend to run a size smaller than domestic. If you'll allow me I can measure you for a better fit.'' 
 
 `` Sure.'' I said, shrugging. 
 
 He motioned for me to raise my arms to the side and then he elongated his arms, snaking them around my body. They went around my neck, under my arms and around my chest, and around my waist. It was more than a little unnerving. 
 
 `` These should be a better fit.'' he reached two display counters over and picked up the same style of shirts I was holding. 
 
 `` Thanks.'' I reply, comparing the differences. The ones he picked were a size larger. I placed them in my anti-grav cart, noticing for the first time the anti-grav plates were shaped like Dr.Robotroid's face; their inventor. 
 
 Next I walked over to the shoe department. I grabbed the display shoe for the one I wanted and tracked down a salesperson. 
 
 `` Do you have this in a size ten?'' I asked. 
 
 `` Let me check the back for you.'' she said, pulling out a large gnarled twig from her belt pouch. She waved it around in the air, going slow and quick in circular motions. The tip glowed a deep green and a glowing, green, slightly translucent fox materialized at her side. She showed the spirit animal the shoe and said `` size 10.'' The apparition bounded through the wall. A moment later it bounded back through the wall with a shoebox inside it. The fox dissappeared completely and the box fell to the floor. The girl picked it up and placed it in my hand. 
 
 `` There you go. If you need anything else just let me know.'' 
 
 I nodded my thanks and went to try them on. They fit pretty well and I added it to the shirts in my cart. I strolled over to electronics there they were having a sale on computer monitors and USB drives. I grabbed a Dr.Robotroid Galaxy Navigator. `` 2 googelflops'' the package read. I hope it transfers files faster than the 1 googelflop I already had. 
 
 I go up to the counter and ask about the monitor I wanted. The guy at the desk typed some things into the computer. `` We have a few left.'' he said. If you'll give me just a second I'll get one for you. 
 
 A second later he dissappeared into thin air and then reappeared with my monitor in his hands. I thanked him, put the monitor in my cart and made my way to the checkout counter. I passed by the sample table from earlier. The girl was still there but the fire boy and the beardo were gone. 
 
 I used a self checkout machine and ticked off the `` Instant Delivery?'' when the option came up. As I bagged my purchases a girl with radient, flaming, orange hair and completely black eyes come up. `` You chose the Instant Delivery Option?'' she said, in a questioning tone. 
 
 `` Yes,'' I reply. `` I can carry them myself.'' The girl confirmed my address and then closed her eyes. She brought her hands close together and a violet ball of energy began to form and grow larger until it filled the space between her hands. I stepped to her side just in case. She flung her hands out in front of her. The energy ball flew out and expanded until it was just a little taller than me. The opaque colour faded away and I saw the door of my house. Then she beckoned me to step through. I did so, feeling my right foot land in the grass on my lawn while my left was still on the tiled floor of the store. As I stepped through completely I heard a voice in the head say `` Thank you for shopping at Super Supermart.''
retelling:
Narrated by The Woman on High Shelf:

In the towering heights of the Super Supermart, nestled amidst rows of boxes and trinkets, I found myself in a peculiar predicament. A cacophony of sounds echoed through the air, a symphony of futuristic hums, beeps, and voices that bordered on overwhelming. My eyes strained to adjust to the vibrant hues illuminated by the ever-present glow of neon lights.

From my lofty perch, I observed a stream of peculiar characters traversing the store. First, there was the enigmatic figure known as Dr. Robotroid, whose groundbreaking anti-grav technology allowed for the floating shopping carts that seemed to defy all laws of physics. Then came the Man in the Costume, a friendly and welcoming presence at the entrance, who greeted each shopper with a radiant smile and a firm handshake.

As I waited, I couldn't help but notice the sibling pair manning the food sample table. The Teenage Girl was ever-cheerful, scooping samples of ice cream into little cups for customers. Her brother, the Teenage Boy with the fiery pyrokinesis, was a constant presence nearby. He kept a watchful eye, ready to deter any would-be harassers like the unkempt man with his inappropriate comments and fiery beard.

The day's most peculiar encounter, however, happened when a customer approached the display counters of the Men's Wear Department. The Young Man in red spandex, our sales associate, extended his unusually long arms to measure him with an air of professionalism. I couldn't help but feel a pang of envy - if only I could stretch my own limbs and reach down for that box I needed!

Little did I know that help was on the way in the form of The Store Employee in battle armour. His rocket boots propelled him through the air, reaching the shelves I couldn't even see from where I stood. He retrieved my box with a flourish and handed it down to me, finally freeing me from my high shelf imprisonment.

As I watched the customers stream by, one caught my eye: a lone figure clad in a plain tunic and trousers. This was The Narrator, our mystery shopper for the day. They navigated the store with ease, witnessing the strange and wondrous sights it had to offer - from the salesperson summoning the Green Fox spirit animal to retrieve items in the back stock room, to the unique self-checkout kiosks where customers could complete their purchases with a simple wave of their hands.

The Narrator eventually made their way to the checkout area, completing their purchase with an electronic scan and paying for their goods at one of the self-checkout machines. Little did they know that this was only the beginning of the store's unique offerings - for their items would soon be transported directly to their home via the magical energy ball of the "Instant Delivery" service.

And so, as the day drew to a close and the store lights began to dim, I couldn't help but feel grateful for my own unique vantage point among the high shelves of the Super Supermart. It was a place of mystery, wonder, and endless amusement - a world apart from the mundane routine below. And as the sounds of shoppers and humming machinery faded away, I prepared myself for another day of bizarre encounters and captivating scenes in this futuristic emporium of dreams.

name: UberFirstDay
source:
“ Don ’ t worry. I can drive, ” he says, glancing at me in the rear-view mirror. 
 
 I ’ m a little worried that my uber driver feels the need to reassure me of this fact. I usually assume when I get into an uber that the driver has a licence, knows the road rules, is proficient in the act of driving… 
 
 I now have some doubts. 
 
 Since he has already pulled away from the curb when he makes this worrisome statement, I ’ m not entirely sure what to do. Do I ask him to explain? Tell him to stop? Take his word for it and hope for the best?! 
 
 Turns out, I don ’ t have to ask him for clarification. 
 
 He continues, “ I ’ m just a bit nervous. First day on the job, y ’ know? Never driven professionally before. ” 
 
 “ Oh, ” I say, “ Well… I ’ m sure you ’ ll do great. You ’ re doing really well so far. ” 
 
 We are stopped at the intersection at the end of my street. We have now been on the road for less than 2 minutes, so this isn ’ t overwhelming praise, but he seems grateful for the compliment. 
 “ Oh yeah? Thanks! That means a lot, ” he exclaims, grinning at me in the rear-view mirror. 
 
 We turn the corner. 
 
 “ No prob- Oh my god! Look out! ” 
 
 My neighbour ’ s fluffy, white, and utterly stupid pomerian is standing in the middle of the road. 
 
 Or rather, it was standing in the middle of the road. 
 
 Fuck.
retelling:
Perspective: The Uber Driver

In the driver's seat of a sleek, silver Uber, a new day begins. The digital map on the dashboard hums softly as I navigate through unfamiliar streets, my fingers gripping the wheel tightly. My heart pounds in my chest like a drum, each beat echoing the rhythm of anticipation and fear.

The first passenger of the day slides into the back seat, their eyes meeting mine via the rear-view mirror. I offer a reassuring smile, attempting to mask the uncertainty that threatens to overwhelm me. "Don't worry," I say, my voice steady despite the quiver in my tone. "I know this route like the back of my hand."

We glide smoothly along the street, the scenery blurring past us in a kaleidoscope of colors and shapes. Suddenly, my eyes lock onto a tiny ball of fluff darting across the road. It's a dog - a Pomeranian, I think - belonging to one of my neighbors. My heart leaps into my throat as I instinctively swerve to avoid it, the car tires screeching in protest.

The dog, thankfully, escapes unscathed and bounds back into its yard, but the near miss leaves me shaken. I let out a sigh of relief, my palms slick with sweat on the wheel. I remind myself that this is just the beginning, that I'll get better with time.

As we continue our journey, I can't help but reflect on the events unfolding before me. I am a driver now - a part of this bustling city's lifeblood. It may be my first day, but I am determined to make it count. The passenger in the back seat remains silent, lost in thought. I glance at them again via the mirror, hoping they are not too disturbed by my close call with their neighbor's four-legged friend.

The city stretches out before us, a vibrant tapestry of sights, sounds, and smells. I am a humble thread in this grand design, a player in the daily drama that unfolds within its confines. And though my heart races and my palms grow sweaty at the thought, I know I'm exactly where I belong - behind the wheel, navigating the city's arteries and veins, and making connections with the passengers who entrust their journeys to me.

name: SixDecadesResistance
source: IT took six decades to form the strength to resist they controlled everything, freedoms defined and histories banned at a global level. The resistance started slowly some graffiti in the corners, a slashed tire a few bolts missing from their machine. Their strength alone defined our weakness they need n't notice such mice. Some of us caved from the doubt we had to watch them for years our lives balanced on secrets. Men of tunnels and sewers costumes and disguise we grew by pain and hunger and ranks swelled and lessons were learned. They could n't ignore the third blast they could n't sign off some gas leak or coincidence our time was now on this day.
retelling:
Narrative Perspective: The Men of Tunnels and Sewers

In the heart of a vast, unyielding global dystopia, where the oppressive regime controlled every aspect of life, we, the men of tunnels and sewers, lived our clandestine existence. Our domain was the subterranean labyrinth beneath the cities, a hidden realm where freedom and resistance thrived unnoticed by those above.

We were mere shadows in the grand tapestry of this oppressive society, faceless entities whose identities were as unknown to them as theirs were to us. We worked tirelessly, carving out our sanctuaries in the dark recesses beneath the concrete jungle.

The air above was a battlefield of ideologies, where rebellion blossomed in small acts of defiance, like graffiti on walls and slashed tires on machines. But for us, it was a different kind of fight—one fought with tools and patience instead of guns and bravado. We were patient soldiers, building the foundation for our eventual open rebellion against the regime.

Six decades passed, as we honed our skills and waited for the right moment to strike. We knew that doubt and hardship would plague us, that despair would threaten to tear us apart. But we held on, driven by a shared desire for freedom and the hope that one day, our struggle would be more than just whispers in the darkness.

That day came when the third, undeniable attack shook the foundations of the regime's control. The act was a testament to the power of unity and resilience. It signaled not only the beginning of open rebellion but also marked our emergence from the shadows. We were no longer just men of tunnels and sewers—we were the heart of the resistance, ready to take on the regime head-on.

As we stepped out into the light, the world above stared back at us with a mixture of surprise and fear. But we knew that this was only the beginning, that our fight for freedom was far from over. We had come a long way in the darkness, but now it was time to lead the charge into the open, where the true battle awaited.

name: JeromeUnirnetEncounter
source:
Jerome lowered himself into his office chair. He stared at his computer monitor with desultory 
 eyes. What's the point? Five months and hundreds of resumes and zero interviews. Blacklisted. 
 Nobody would touch him. His mouth grimaced bitterly. His wife had n't touched him for four of 
 those months. She spent her time working late shifts at the hospital now to provide for him. 
 Provide for. What a stupid concept. 
 
 The monitor's glow was warm. Jerome could feel the ire in him ebb a little in the face of the 
 ambient glow. So what if he could n't get a job. So what if the sink was full of dishes he 
 dirtied while Sharon slaved for the worthless food he burned on them. So what if he was being 
 subjected to an FBI investigation. So what if his psychiatrist did n't think he could handle his case any longer. None of that mattered right now, he and his computer had the 
 whole night, everything else could come crashing back in in the morning. 
 
 As Jerome's eyes focused, his brain struggled to catch up. He ran through the usual checklist of 
 social media, message boards, and pornography. Two hours had passed before, after a bittersweet 
 release, his mind snapped into place. He began running programs, mostly of his own making and 
 all with his own alterations, and cruising through the real internet. A little banking 
 information here ( useless ), preliminary specifications for an unreleased and unannounced video 
 game, and more data than he could look at in a lifetime on the side. The hours drifted by with 
 an endless quickness that made Jerome feel out of time's grasp, rubberbanding between muted 
 dread and sedate immortality. He was a demigod of the digital, stuck between the electronic and 
 the macro-physical. 
 
 At nearly three AM Jerome's mundanity reasserted itself. His bladder was full and his stomach 
 was growling. Ridiculous. He urinated into the small garbage can and ate a handful of caramel 
 popcorn from a large decorative tin under Sharon's desk in the office they shared. She would n't 
 notice, it had been there since last Christmas. A gift from her ever frowning, ever working 
 parents. Maybe he'd empty the garbage before she got home. 
 
 As he sank back into his inner world, no, his outer world, the internet was the most `` out'' 
 Jerome could achieve, he felt a modicum of peace leech back into him. He drifted for another 
 hour or so until he stumbled upon something odd. A program had found its way into, through a 
 series of connections that were odd in themselves, something called `` Unirnet.'' He spent the next 
 twenty minutes working his way inside this Unirnet. Upon doing so, the browser he was using 
 displayed nothing but garbled text for a moment before scripts began running. He tried to follow 
 along for a moment before launching countermeasures. However, much to his startlement and 
 building chagrin, everything failed. As he was about to disconnect manually a window appeared on 
 his screen. `` Translation and integration complete! Welcome, user, to Unirnet!'' Jerome mouthed 
 the words, `` translation and integration,'' and as he was again about to disconnect the window 
 closed and he was looking at a page of English words. It appeared to be an information hub with 
 links to hundreds of things like, `` Government, Food, Interpersonal Relationships, Contests, 
 Sensory Stimulation, Upload,'' and so on overlayed over a slightly quivering background that hurt 
 his eyes a little. 
 
 `` What am I looking at here?'' Jerome asked aloud as curiosity took hold. He selected `` Sensory 
 Stimulation'' and waited a moment as it began loading. It loaded slowly before coming up only 
 with the words, `` Hardware Not Found.'' He frowned and went back to the hub and selected 
 `` Government.'' The page again loaded slowly. However, this time, upon completion it was filled 
 with another hub with links superimposed over an emblem that appeared to be what he thought a 
 palm tree crossed with penises might look like placed over a bluish orb. Under the emblem were 
 the words, `` Loosely Associated Governments and Holdings.'' Jerome remembered the bit about the 
 translation and briefly considered that he was truly reading a direct translation of something 
 else. Again it was all over the slightly quivering background that made it difficult to focus 
 too closely on the screen. He looked over the hundreds of links available before backing to the 
 central hub again. 
 
 This time he tried a link titled simply, `` Food.'' He was again greeted with another hub that had 
 so many links, which all seemed to lead to more hubs, that he felt overwhelmed. He tried 
 following some of the links and did find end points with what looked like recipes and 
 discussions and descriptions and slowly loading.jpegs that would appear after lengthy instances 
 of `` translating and integrating.'' Some of the pictures looked almost familiar, like one instance 
 that looked something like a wet pineapple. Most, however, seemed like something conceived of in 
 a diseased mind Jerome imagined one would only find lurking inside of most FBI agents or 
 corporate executives. It was nearly morning now and Susan would be home soon. Not yet. Still 
 time for a little more looking. 
 
 Jerome tried `` Interpersonal Relationships'' next. Susan? Sharon might have found this one 
 informative, he thought. He found hub after hub of listings for what looked like different types 
 of peoples and interests. He tried one called `` Seeking Intercranial Stimulation Through Invasive 
 Penetration.'' The dry but euphemistic article was clearly some kind of oddly worded 
 solicitation. After a moment he clicked on the reply link at the bottom and watched a text entry 
 box drop down. After scratching his crotch momentarily he typed in, `` Hello. What is 
 `` Intercranial Stimulation?'' He wondered what basement in what country, if this was n't simply a 
 cosmetic feature, his message would be sent to. He himself used to sit in front of his computer 
 in college and compose entries for an encyclopedic fake agency that handled the containment of 
 fictional horrors. He wondered why he had never heard of Unirnet before now. Why would anyone go 
 to all of this trouble and then bury all of the work where nobody would ever see it? 
 
 As he was backing out of hubs again, a small window popped up with a link `` Open Message.'' A 
 reply to his reply? He again thought of diseased minds when he considered the type of person 
 that would handle messaging with pop-up windows. He clicked the link. After a very lengthy load 
 that he monitored closely another window opened and a video began to play. At first he had 
 trouble making it out. It had a strange quality as though it was shot through a thin jelly. 
 There was also a strange sloshing sound playing. He realized he was looking at what almost 
 appeared to be a face except it was more like a series of different holes aligned on a pallid 
 and taught skin. The way it moved, the way the holes moved ever so slightly made him feel very 
 uncomfortable. His discomfort knew no bounds, however, when a series of what looked like 
 slightly hooked tentacles invaded those holes and his speakers emitted a crackling, crooning 
 sound that made his teeth ache. He closed the video immediately to find another message. 
 `` Interested? I am ready to receive penetration at any time, my delightful brood mate.'' Jerome 
 closed that too. He was n't thinking of basement dwelling programmers anymore. He wondered if 
 Suzanne might like breakfast today. He could wash the dishes and make it before she got home, 
 there was time. Instead, he backed to the central hub again. 
 
 He stared at it awhile, watching the quivering background more closely, feeling his head ache. 
 He clicked on `` Upload'' this time and again got a message about hardware not being found. This 
 time he tried clicking on the message and was rewarded with another hub that appeared to lead to 
 online storefronts selling something only called an `` Interface.'' He clicked on one selection and 
 saw a lot of descriptors about ease of use and prompt delivery. The part about `` no surgical 
 intervention'' was interesting. He clicked again, this time on `` Deliver to Me'' and was redirected 
 to a page stating `` Location new, contact not established. Delivery will be delayed until contact 
 is made. Loosely Associated Governments and Holdings Office of Contact will communicate a 
 petition of membership to your local government. Please enjoy your Interface upon arrival on 
 behalf of Minds Incorporated Manufacturing Consortium. We are hungry for your business.'' 
 
 Jerome pushed back from his computer, his head pounding. His face felt hot, like he'd been in 
 the sun too long. Maybe he will make that breakfast for Sally. Samantha? He put a hand to his 
 face as he stood and afterwards looked dully at the blood from his nose that had collected on 
 his fingers. His eyes stung a little. He could get the dishes done before she got home from the 
 pharmacy, at least. Maybe the DEA would call him and tell him the charges had been dropped. He'd 
 probably get a call about an accounting job today. He did n't go to college to sit at home all 
 day looking at websites. Maybe he should order another Interface for what's-her-name.
