name: CoastalPayback
source:
The calm before the storm pushes goosebumps to the skin like the tilted carriage of a roller coaster. I stand between the boulder formations of a seaside ridge, watching the frost white clouds churn the ocean into crystals. A wave becomes an explosive generator, de-misting as giant blue shark teeth in the ocean's maw. Evacuate was the news reader's sermon. But if seeing true beauty is worth a lifetime, then I choose to wash away as part of the rocky shore. 
 
 The gusts howl against the frozen sea and sky. Dark blue pools reach up and mingle with angry clouds of grey. The closer the storm comes, the more it seems like an artist splashing shades of blue and black on tapestry. My only assurance that this is real, is the burning cold on each fingertip. 
 
 The sky flashes silver, sending vibrations through my toes and up my spine. The furious Poseidon, God, or Allah is finally out to exact revenge upon us. 
 
 For years we tossed human waste and offloaded faeces like fish food without batting an eye. To disgrace a fellow man is a tragedy, but the world wilts away with our pride. 
 
 The experts name it hurricane, super storm, and freak of nature. I am here, lips chapped from frost, fingers shivering, and insides melting into ice. This is no mistake, no freak show or art gallery exhibit. 
 
 It is payback time and we are on the chopping block. The difference between beauty and God's revenge is in the eye of the perceiver. Do not tell me to run when we have lived all our lives with pride. I face my maker and am duly judged for my crimes.
retelling:
From the Perspective of Poseidon, the Greek God of the Sea:

In the vast expanse of my domain, a storm brews, an ominous testament to humanity's transgressions against the Earth. I, Poseidon, the Lord of the Seas and Earthquakes, have decided to show mankind the power they've disregarded for too long.

A human, daringly perched on a rocky ridge, gazes upon the impending tempest, his eyes reflecting awe and acceptance. He chooses to stay, embracing the spectacle of my wrath. I, in turn, reveal the full fury of my realm, the ocean's frost-white crests crashing against the rocky shores with the force of giant blue shark teeth.

I observe as the human feels the bitter cold and the raw power that is my storm. He ponders the years of pollution and disregard for the planet, understanding, finally, the consequences of his actions. The human accepts his fate, submitting to the destructive force I have unleashed.

From the sky above, a cascade of silver flashes illuminates the darkening skies, casting eerie shadows over my churning waters. I, Poseidon, have spoken, and the Earth listens. This storm is not just retribution, but a warning for the future. Let humanity remember that I am the master of the seas, and they are mere mortals who must respect the power of nature.

name: JimsFortiethDeparture
source:
The day had finally come. It was October 3rd and Jim was turning 40. He woke up just as he had every other day of his life. Nothing had changed – not really. He had always known this was coming and had never dreamt it wouldn ’ t be so. Why hope for a miracle? Why should he bother imagining ways the assembly line could fail? It never did. 
 
 The city churned out babies like the factories produced cars, television sets, food and everything else. Jim didn ’ t look back as he left his tiny, standardized apartment for the last time. He walked through the busy, smog filled streets, chuckling at the hustle and bustle of those not yet turned 40. They were digging their own graves. This wasn ’ t a revelation but rather something Jim had always known. He was sure they all knew it as well. They were granted life by the same city that would take it away 40 years later. This life force was merely loaned to every citizen so that they can repay the city in full. Jim had finally finished repaying his debt. 
 
 As Jim made his way to the edge of the city, he presented the necessary credentials to the guard. His ID noted him an engineer at the “ Air Purification Facility. ” It was one of many government owned facilities like it, tasked with maintaining the pollutants at life-permitting levels. Jim was granted access outside of the city and was handed a filtration mask; he would need it outside the city where toxic pollutants pervaded the atmosphere. 
 
 Once he found his way a few miles outside of the city, he took off the mask. He took a few deep breaths that were more full of life than any before. He no longer owed anyone anything. His life was his own.
retelling:
Narrated by **The Guard**:

   On that day, as the clock struck noon under the smog-laden sky, I stood at my post, a symbol of the city's ironclad order. The face before me belonged to Jim, an engineer at one of our own facilities, a cog in the grand machinery that kept this city running.

   He approached with a determined stride, his eyes filled with a resolve I had not seen in many years. His credentials were in order, as they always were, but there was something different about him today. A spark, perhaps, or maybe just the weight of decades bearing down on him.

   As he handed over the required documents and waited for my nod of approval, I could see the anticipation building within him. This wasn't just another day at work; this was a rite of passage, the final act in a life scripted since birth.

   With a curt nod, I granted him exit from our city - a place that gave life and took it away with equal efficiency. He accepted his filtration mask, a symbol of his bondage until now, and then walked towards the gate. As he stepped beyond its threshold, he removed the mask, casting off the shackles of his servitude.

   I watched as he disappeared into the haze, heading towards the unknown. In that moment, I felt a pang of envy. Envy for the freedom he had just found, the adventure that lay ahead, and the possibility of creating a life beyond the city's boundaries.

   Here I remain, bound by duty and loyalty to this city that both nurtures and consumes us. But today, I dreamt of the day when I too could break free from these chains, find my own autonomy, and embrace whatever awaited me on the other side.

name: JohnsGriefAndAbdul
source:
`` John... Jooohn..?? John!'' his mother shouted as he had another one of his moments. 2 weeks, 2 weeks and 3 days since his brother, Danial had passed away. He never expected this to happen, he always thought that since he was 7 years older he'd be the one to die first, and therefore spare himself of going through anything like this, `` JOHN?! ``, his mother continued, so she could to make him answer, and stop daydreaming in the bathroom. To her surprise, however, he just looked at her and with the calmest voice ever said `` Yes mum?'' 
 `` It's time, the ceremony is about to start'' After a brief 10-second silence, he unlocked the door of that bathroom and with tears in his eyes he managed to smile at how pathetic all of this was. This is a ceremony for Danis clothes, but not the person Dani, the one whom he loved so much, his best friend. How can NASA not find a human body within the ISS??, he thought, does n't make any fucking sense. This was something that he has been expressing for everyone the past 2 weeks. Just before they entered the main room he mumbled `` let's just get this over with 
 
 Later that evening, Katrine, his mother who decided to stay over at his house got a call, but it was n't for her, but for John. `` John! You got your friend Abdul asking for you!'' 
 
 
 Abdul? Who's Abdul? He thought as he picked up the phone 
 
 J: `` Hello?'' 
 
 A: `` John, meet me at 14th Adams Ave. now.'' 
 
 J: `` Who is this?'' 
 
 A: `` Yo, you wan na know the truth or not?'' 
 
 J:'' The truth? About what?'' 
 
 A:'' Meet me and I'll explain'' 
 
 The person hung up. John stood there, as confused as ever thinking if he should go to Adams Ave. or not. It's soon midnight, the only people there should be people queuing up to get into the club. His curiosity got to him. He quickly got his tracksuit on and got ready. `` Adams Ave. is only 10 minutes by bike, that should be fairly quick, nothing dangerous or so, even if it's this late.'' he thought nervously as he went out. Not a single word from his mother, who was just happy that he's finally out with a friend. `` I guess I'll drink myself to sleep alone'' she mumbled to herself. 
 
 As John took his bike, he knew exactly the way there and arrived at Adams Ave. Nothing unusual, the predicted club queue was there, and some drunk people shouting cheerfully about how happy they are. Good old Adams Ave. As time passed by, he remembered that he'd had to go to 14th Adams Ave., which is another 2 minutes from Adams Ave. When John was finally there, briefly sweaty after that rough bike-session. John looks around and finds no one, until a door from the building in front of him opens and he hears Abdul's voice go `` We've been expecting you John.''

Perspective: Katrine (John's mother)

In the quiet solitude of her home, Katrine found herself preoccupied by the recent loss of her beloved son, Daniel. Two weeks had passed since that fateful day, yet the emptiness lingered, a palpable void in the once bustling household. The house seemed to hum with an eerie silence, every creak and groan echoing with the weight of her sorrow.

On this particular evening, however, the house was filled with a different kind of noise - the soft murmurs of a gathering. A ceremony had been arranged for Daniel's clothes, a tradition that held deep significance in their family, but one that Katrine could hardly bear. Her other son, John, stood amidst the group, his eyes distant and unfocused, as if he were a million miles away - perhaps on the International Space Station where Daniel had met his end.

As the ceremony drew to a close, Katrine could sense John's frustration and disbelief seeping through the cracks in his stoic facade. She wished she could comfort him, but words seemed insufficient in such a moment. Instead, she clung to the hope that somehow, some way, they would find answers about Daniel's untimely death.

Later that night, as the house settled into its usual stillness, Katrine heard John's footsteps heading out of the house. Her heart skipped a beat; was he going out so late? A call from someone named Abdul had drawn him away from the sanctuary of their home. Katrine couldn't help but feel a pang of worry for her son, but there was nothing she could do except pray for his safety and hope that this mysterious encounter would bring some semblance of closure to their grief-stricken hearts.

name: DaddysBigBalloon
source:
Dear Diary, 
 
 Daddy took me to work with him today. He said it was a great achievement for us but all I saw was a big balloon. When it filled up everybody started clapping. Then they deflated it! What good is a balloon when it's not blown up? I do n't understand what daddy does at work but mommy said that its gon na change the way we travel. She said there will be no more cars or airplanes, everyone will fly in giant balloons! I thought that sounded fun! When we got home mommy made a big dinner for us, it was a good day. Goodnight diary. 
 
 -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- 
 
 Dear Diary, 
 
 What a day! Daddy was home already when I got back from school, and he took me to the fair! He's been so happy since his balloon worked. He said tomorrow we get to see it fly! I'm so excited I ca n't wait, I wan na fly and see the clouds and birds! I do n't want to wait, I want to go right now. But mommy says I have to rest so I can enjoy it. Goodnight diary! 
 
 -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- 
 
 Dear Diary, 
 
 Today was not a good day. Me and Mommy went to meet Daddy at work to see his big balloon fly. Everything was fun but then something happened and then there was fire. The balloon started deflating and it crashed! Everyone was screaming and running, but it's just a balloon. Mommy is still in the living room crying and Daddy has n't come home yet. I should probably go to sleep.
retelling:
Narrative Perspective: The Balloon (Inanimate Object Point of View)

Under the vast expanse of the sky, I, a colossal balloon, began my journey at Daddy's workplace - an expansive testing ground where dreams take flight and innovation reigns supreme. I was filled with gas, rising higher, larger, my vibrant colors contrasting against the azure backdrop.

Daddy, a man of ambition and ingenuity, had breathed life into me, hoping to revolutionize travel. The mother, with her eyes wide and full of wonder, suggested that I symbolized the future - a promise of adventure and exploration beyond the horizons.

The child observed my inflation and deflation, his curiosity piqued by the spectacle unfolding before him. Excitement rippled through me as the successful test concluded, and Daddy took pride in his creation. He spoke to the child about the thrill of tomorrow's demonstration, his eyes sparkling with anticipation.

The next day, I floated above the fairgrounds - a place brimming with laughter and joy. The child's eyes twinkled as he rode rides and indulged in sweets. Daddy, too, was filled with exhilaration, eager to share his vision with the world.

However, fate had other plans. In the early hours of the following morning, I found myself enveloped by the darkness, drifting towards a field or specially designed test site - my final destination. The demonstration began, and though I tried to soar gracefully through the air, a catastrophic malfunction occurred.

A deafening roar echoed across the landscape as flames engulfed me. The child's screams pierced the chaos, tearing at Daddy's heart. He tried to rush towards the burning inferno, but it was too late. I had failed in my mission, and my existence now lay shrouded in tragedy.

In the aftermath, the mother cried, her sobs echoing through the house as Daddy remained absent, consumed by guilt and grief over his creation's demise. The child, though unharmed, was left with a haunting memory of the spectacle that ended in disaster. And I, once symbolizing hope, now stood as a reminder of the unpredictable nature of innovation and the heavy toll it can take on those who dare to dream.

name: cityMonsterDeath
source:
Death and destruction was everywhere I looked. The sounds of crumbling buildings and breaking glass were ringing. The stench of blood was overpowering. I just wanted to go home, but I could n't walk away from him- from *it*. 
 
 It was a monster. That was the only way to describe it. Killing and destroying everything in its path. What was its path anyway? It did n't seem to care. Like a tornado or hurricane, it was a force of nature. No motivation, no evil plans, it just *was*. 
 
 I sat at the center of the city, clutching my sword and clearing my throat. My sword could cut through anything, and my voice had the potential to cause untold destruction. But that was just it: they were tools for death, which was why I had sworn never to use them again. I felt I was becoming something I did n't want to be. Almost like this monster. And who would be here to stop me? 
 
 The ground shook. It was getting closer. I could start to see it in the distance, the louder its steps became. Closing my eyes, I took in a deep breathe as I tightened my grip on the sword. As I exhaled, I stood up and ran. Full speed ahead, lifting the sword high into the air. I yelled. As loud as I possibly could. The monster locked eyes with me and gave off a terrifying, grievous yell of its own. As we sped toward each other, I opened my mouth. 
 
 `` *Death! *'' I yelled, the sound echoing in all directions. The monster stumbled, but remained unfazed. That's never happened before. The word has never left anyone standing. I kept running, my hand ached, but I held on. 
 
 The monster leapt into the air, arcing into a downward spiral toward me. I repositioned the sword as it ended its descent, pushing with all my might. It ripped into its flesh, impaling through its chest. If I thought its war cries were loud, its cries of anguish were deafening. Within a few moments, it was replaced with silence as it fell to the ground. 
 
 I breathed a sigh of relief. The nightmare was over. But I had taken a life when I promised I would never raise my sword again. It was intoxicating though, a feeling missing for a long time. I did n't want to let it go.
retelling:
From the perspective of the Monster:

In the heart of a shattered city, where echoes of destruction reverberated through crumbling buildings and streets lay strewn with debris, I found myself awakening. The stench of decay and death filled my senses, a familiar scent that seemed to follow me everywhere. My path of chaos, etched into the very fabric of this forsaken place, led me to an unexpected encounter.

A figure stood defiantly at the heart of the carnage, a warrior clad in armor, wielding a powerful sword and bearing a voice that echoed like thunder. I knew not who he was, nor what purpose he served, but his presence held a strange allure. He had vowed never to use that mighty sword again, or so the whispers went, yet here we were, facing each other in a dance as old as time itself.

His battle cry, "Death!", rang out like a clarion call, and for a moment, I staggered under its weight. Yet, the power of my own being was too great to be swayed by such a feeble challenge. With a roar that shook the very ground beneath our feet, I pressed forward, heedless of the destruction in my wake.

The warrior's sword flashed with an eerie light as it met my hide, sparking and spattering crimson across the ruined landscape. Each blow seemed to shatter my resolve, yet I could not be stopped. My path was one of destruction, and nothing would deter me from following its course.

Finally, the warrior struck true, a fatal wound that should have ended my existence. But something within me twisted and writhed, defying death itself. With one final, agonized bellow, I collapsed, defeated but unbroken.

As the warrior gazed upon his handiwork, a look of relief crossed his features, yet it was tinged with a darkness that spoke of deeper turmoil. His voice, once a beacon of hope, now echoed with an intoxicating power that I could feel even in my weakened state. It seemed our dance had only just begun.

name: BootsAndVoices
source:
`` Stop treading on me'' My boots said. 
 
 God, will you please shut the fuck up for nine fucking seconds I thought as I stabbed the sentry in the neck, beginning a chain reaction of voices crying out, my own knife letting out a long surprised `` whooooaaaaa'' as it plunged into the man's cream uniform. It was his own fault I had found him out here, his pants had been expressing the discomfort of laying on the rocky ground when my squad had been coming around the corner. I wiped my knife off on the man's shoulder, my knife giving a sputter from lips that were n't real. 
 
 `` Could have given me a little warning first'' The knife said from my shoulder. 
 
 The taped ball of my dog tags agreed with a muffled groan from my chest. 
 
 `` I said no talking out on patrol, that means no talking'' I whisper to them as my squad formed up behind me. 
 
 I stopped as the wind rustled through the valley, a soft snore arising from my BDUs. At least they would sleep. I could n't wear my knee pads or the elbow pads on patrol anymore, the giggles they had were as frustrating as the dog tags. I slide my rifle around my front, it gave a long hiss out of the suppressor at the front. He was always a whiny bastard, hated me, said I always pushed his buttons. I could hear the voices from the bullets inside my magazine. 
 
 `` It's dark in here'' 
 `` It's wet in here'' 
 
 My Sergeant taps me on the arm and all at once the world gets a little quieter. The voices cut out as he turns to me. They always stop when I talk to someone, they interject when I go out alone. 
 
 `` Back on point, Lucky'' He says. 
 
 I nod my head, drawing back the charging handle of my rifle. I see the head of the cartridge poking out of the breech. 
 
 `` Hey do n't put me back in!'' It cried out. 
 
 I dropped the handle and readied the rifle. I wish I had friends. 
 
 `` That was kind of a dick move'' Said the tree I was crouched behind. 
 
 `` Fuck you'' I say as I start forward. 
 
 I wish I had more friends. My boots gurgle as I step through a muddy ditch. The tall grass whipped through the air before me in the voices of children, their voices distant and far away. Friends keep the voices back. My boots are spitting now, spitting from lips that are n't real. But friends are hard to come by in Vietnam. 
 
 `` I see the bad moon rising. I see trouble on the way'' My knife starts to sing as we advance into the jungle.
retelling:
**Perspective: The Boots**

   In the heart of a war-torn Vietnam, I found myself attached to the feet of Lucky, a soldier whose boots I would come to know intimately. Each day, we trudged through the mud and muck, the dampness seeping into my leather layers, the salt of sweat mixing with the grime.

   I could hear the rifle next to me, its metallic voice heavy with tension, echoing Lucky's anxiety. The knife clanked against his belt, sharp and unyielding, always ready for action. His dog tags jangled a melody that was more ominous than comforting. Each of them had their own voices, their own stories, and they shared them openly with the world.

   Lucky moved through the tall grass, his uniform rustling like whispers in the wind. The grass itself seemed to be filled with children's laughter, a strange and disconcerting sound in this place of death and destruction. We were all connected, part of the same tragic symphony, each note resonating with a different tone but blending together into one haunting melody.

   One day, Lucky stopped. He stood still for a moment before lifting his rifle and firing. A sentry fell to the rocky ground, a life extinguished in an instant. The silence that followed was deafening, but it didn't last long. His knife groaned, his dog tags wept, and even I felt a pang of sorrow.

   Lucky tried to silence us, but we were relentless in our chatter. We spoke of the mud underfoot, the wind rustling through the valley, and the jungle that lay ahead. He grew frustrated, trying to shut us up, but we persisted. We were more than just boots or a knife or dog tags; we were his companions, his confidants in this hellish landscape.

   The Sergeant's voice rang out, a temporary respite from our incessant chatter. But even he couldn't silence the emptiness that gnawed at Lucky's soul. We were reminders of the life he had left behind, echoes of the friends he had lost, whispers of the horror that surrounded him.

   As we moved deeper into the jungle, my steps echoed with a new rhythm. The knife began to hum an ominous tune, its notes intertwining with the rustling of leaves and the distant sounds of gunfire. We were marching towards an uncertain future, bound together by duty, sorrow, and the unyielding reality of war.

   And so, we continued our journey, Lucky and I, each step taking us further into the heart of darkness, bound by a shared history and the haunting symphony of a battlefield.

name: devilsDeal
source:
You're sitting in your office chair, at your high-powered job. You have three years left, and by god you're going to enjoy them. You pull the packet out of your sport-jacket pocket, gingerly unzip it, and sprinkle some of the contents on the table. You cut it into four lines, and start snorting. You look up after the second line, and it's *him*. 
 
 Your blood runs cold, before the rush hits you. 
 
 `` Enjoying yourself, James? ``, he asks sardonically. 
 
 When you used to picture the devil, he was red-skinned with hooves and a pitchfork, or a suave man in a business suit, perhaps. Not even close. He's an old man with a crooked smile and a bowler hat, with a gaudy ruby ring on his left ring finger. He's leaning forward on a thin black cane with a red handle. 
 
 `` You've done well for yourself, or, I should say, I've done well for you. But, regrettably, something has come up.'' 
 
 He looks at you with a frown. You're sweating profusely, now. Is he taking you early? Fuck. FUCK. 
 
 `` I'm'offering' you a new deal. Your soul back, for one favor.'' 
 
 You're speechless, at first. 
 
 `` W-What do you want, Master? ``, you manage to stammer out, heart pounding from cocaine and terror. 
 
 `` I need you to hire someone. My son.'' 
 
 He hands you a C.V., and you're taken aback. It's blank, except for a name and a picture. You gather your courage. 
 
 `` Is this a joke?'' 
 
 He stares at you with beady eyes. You blink and look away. 
 
 ``... Send him up. ``, you manage. 
 
 He tips his hat and smiles, before disappearing. No noise, or special effect. He's just gone. 
 
 You reach under your desk, hands passing over your gun and finding your bottle of whisky. 
 
 With unsteady hands, you pour yourself a drink.
retelling:
Perspective: The Devil's Son (unnamed)

In the heart of a bustling city, cloaked within the confines of an unassuming high-powered office, I found myself waiting, my eyes fixed on the man seated behind the desk. A seasoned executive, with three years left before retirement, he was known as James. My father, The Devil, had sent me to him.

The atmosphere in this office was thick with tension and the pungent aroma of cocaine. As I stood there, my heart raced. This man held the key to my future. My name, a faceless entity on the CV in his hands, my face staring back at him from its corner, was all that connected me to this world.

From the shadows, The Devil emerged, an old man with a crooked smile and a bowler hat, adorning his head like a sinister crown. A gaudy ruby ring sparkled on his finger, the symbol of my family's power. With a wave of his hand, he startled James out of his stupor.

"James," The Devil began, "We have a deal. But I offer you a new proposition. Your soul in exchange for hiring my son." He gestured towards me, the only clue as to who I was.

I could see the fear and shock in James's eyes, but also something else - curiosity, perhaps. The old man's offer was as intriguing as it was terrifying. And yet, with a swift nod, James agreed. A drink was poured, whisky sloshing against the glass, as he seemed to be coping with this strange turn of events.

For me, this was just the beginning. The deal was sealed, and I was one step closer to entering this world. But what awaited me here, in this office, was a mystery yet to unfold.

name: NightmareBodySwap
source:
I wake up in the middle of the night, shaking, drenched in sweat. My chest hurts, my entire body is aching and twitching. The pain flows through my torso to my limbs, waves of heat and soreness let me clench myself into a ball. *'' Fuck! I'm having a heartattack? At the damn age of 17? `` *, I think, as the next wave stings my body from the inside out, leaving me no option other than to give up my position. I feel like I am tied to four horses, pulling my limbs from my body. But the most pain still centers in my chest and between my legs. To the near unbearable heat my chest feels like someone pushes my ribcage out of my -probably soon to be dead- body, while my genitals seem to think the only way to outlive the rest of my body is to force it's way into said body. Paralysed by the pain and the heat, I pray to every God I know about, that they should have merci and hopefully, my inner organs will not burst out as far away as they seem to desire. 
 With the next shockwave flows through my body, the last one before everything turns black. 
 
 I wake up, drenched in sweat like I just ran a million miles. Dizzy and still not fully awake, I shake my head. *'' Damnit, I did n't know a freaking dream could feel this real! Felt like I was about to burst. `` *, I complain to myself, as I try to get up and out of my new water bed. But even the motion of swinging my legs out of the bed nearly ends in a disaster, as I kick them way to powerful and almost fling my lamp off the little nightstand. *'' What the bloody...? Well, that's a fucking fantastic start in a long weekend...'' * But then I hasitate. Something feels... off. I ca n't place my finger on what it is exactly, but my whole body feels... wierd. My legs and arms feel too light, my chest feels a good bit heavier and my waist and everything below seems to be completely out of proportion. 
 I know, there is a lot human psychology can do, but for a dream to have this effect after I wake up? That's just mad! 
 
 I shake my head in disbelief and jump out of my bed as I do so. Something stroked me! I'm by myself this weekend, so surely, a spider must've jumped onto me while I slept! 
 I try to grab it and I even manage to get a hold of the hairy bastard. But as I try to throw it against the wall, my hand gets held back and with incredible pain, my head gets pulled back, almost hard enought for me to fall back in my drenched bed. 
 With that, I finally snap out of my dormant state. I just... pulled on my own hair. That goes way further over my back as it should. With uncertain movements, I stroke over the hair I just nearly ripped out of my head and examine the length. It goes the entire length of my back, stopping just before my bottom. And it feels wierd, somehow thinner... I start to panic. This is not my god damn hair! Whatever happend, if my hair is really that long, I probably was in fucking coma for damn years! Which, as I stumble into the bathroom, would also explain why I ca n't control my body in any way. I do n't know how I survived being in coma for this long, but damn- 
 The moment I look into my mirror, in an effort to calm my panicing self, takes my breath away. I am in front of that mirror, as I were every day for so many years. But instead of a grumpy looking, unhappy guy with a never clean shaved beart, the mirror shows me a delicate, fragile girl, with a red face and eyes staring at me with panic and confusion. 
 I open my mouth, which the girl in the mirror copies. Our eyes simultaniously grow bigger, as neither of us seemed to expect the other one on this wierd morning. 
 I close my eyes, and breath calmly while counting from ten to zero. 
 *'' This ca n't be happening. I... what? I mean... what?! Okay. There, there. I will open my eyes, and when I do, the same ugly face will look back to me as it does every morning. I'm just not really awake now, that's all. `` * 
 
 I sigh and open my eyes. 
 The girl in the mirror seems just as dazed as I feel. 
 She has long, golden hair, a face like a porcelain doll with deep-blue eyes and full lips. Her head is caried by a neck, that seems frail and the rest of what I see in the mirror is her upper body, hiding in a worn out old black shirt. I release my breath, which I appenrently held for the entire time I looked at the girl in the mirror. And she is not less surprised than I am. 
 I a trancelike state, I move my hand up to my torso. As if I want to disprove the thought that starts to manifest in my head, I place my hand on my chest. Only for it to be stopped by something squishy and sensitive. Finally I stop staring at the mirror. I look down on my body, just to see, that my hand actually grab a soft, rather small boob. Of which I do in fact have two. And I suspect, not seeing a bump in my pants is showing me, that not only my morning wood is missing today. 
 
 *'' I'm a god damn girl! `` *

Sorry for wrong gramma and potentialy very wierd sentences, it is very late here and this was a in-one-go thing. I am too tired to edit it at the moment and if this account does n't get deleted for this massive post, I will edit it when I am actually awake. 
 Also sorry for taking this long to even get to the realization, it's probably very uninteresting...

name: HellboundHighway
source:
A blinking light. A repeating beep. The smell of sterile halls. 
 
 So I survived. 
 
 I knew I should n't have tried driving home without snow tires. I've done that trip dozens of times. I know every turn. I told myself I would drive slowly and everything would be fine. 
 
 The truck ahead of me fishtailed and spun. Bang, it hit the median. I tried to avoid it but in this weather we had about as much traction as hockey pucks. 
 
 “ He lives! ” said a calm voice. She chuckled as if he had made a joke. I tried to focus on her voice but my eyes were having trouble adjusting. 
 
 “ Where am I? ” I managed. 
 
 “ Um, let's not start with that ”. She smiled. “ Just relax for now. You've been through a lot ”. 
 
 “ I remember the crash ”. I rubbed my neck. 
 
 “ Really? What do you remember? ” 
 
 “ The truck hit me. My car went upside down. There was fire. I was... I was burning ”. My hands instinctively went to my face, expecting bandages. “ How...? ” 
 
 “ Ok, just relax ”. She grasped my hands and looked in my eyes. “ Normally we would wait until you recovered more, but I do n't think we can avoid it now ”. My eyes narrowed. 
 
 “ Avoid what? ” 
 
 “ Ok so, the crash was worse than you think ”. 
 
 *Fuck, I'm paralyzed*. I immediately tried moving my toes. No, that's not it. 
 
 “ Just tell me what happened ”. 
 
 “ Better yet, I'll show you. That's the only way you'll believe it ”. She walked over to the large window and waved me over. I stood up, with surprisingly little difficulty, and joined her. 
 
 “ Why are n't I sore? How did I not break anything? ” 
 
 “ Just look ”. She pulled back the shades. 
 
 The window opened onto a view unlike anything I had ever seen. A sparkling city extended to the horizon, many-colored buildings reaching for a sky that did not exist. There were no stars, no clouds, nothing. Only a black emptiness with a single bright point at the very center. 
 
 She smiled at my reaction. 
 
 “ I always enjoy this part ”. 
 
 “ Where the fuck am I? ” 
 
 “ Ok, so here's the thing. You mentioned an accident? Well, you did n't survive that ”. 
 
 “ What are you... ” 
 
 “ Just let me finish. You died, I'm sorry. We normally try to take this part slower but something tells me it's better to just rip of the bandage with you ”. 
 
 “ I see. So I'm in Heaven ”. 
 
 “ Thank God, no ”. She laughed again, clearly finding herself hilarious. “ Look outside again. Look at the ground ”. 
 
 Towering skyscrapers reached for the black, some of them disappearing into its inky depths. As my eyes followed them down I realized that we were quite high up. In fact, I could barely make out the ground. Only a reddish glow. 
 
 “ What's down there? ” 
 
 “ Sulfur, mostly. And lava. And demons. It's not a nice place ”. 
 
 “ Wait, I'm in Hell? How the fuck did that happen? I'm a good person. I would n't hurt a fly, I would n't... ” 
 
 “ Just relax ”, she looked into my eyes. “ Do n't worry, things are n't what you think. Yes, this is Hell. But that's not a bad thing. I mean, it certainly used to be. There was a time when living in Hell meant never-ending torment. It meant being boiled alive in lava, choking in sulfur clouds, and being torn apart by demons endlessly ”. 
 
 I swallowed. This did n't sound good so far. 
 
 “ But it was n't endless. You see, a certain kind of person goes to Hell. Hell was n't built for bad people, per se. It was built for those who reject God. Or a god. Or the gods. Whatever your people believed in ”. 
 
 “ Ok, that sounds like the Hell I learned about in Sunday school, more or less ”. 
 
 “ Yes, but think about it. What happens when you put billions of skeptics in one place? Billions of people who rejected faith? You get a population with a high percentage of people who do n't accept what they're told. People who examined their society and found it wanting. People who are n't satisfied with the way things are ”. 
 
 “ I think you might have me confused. I'm not a scientist or writer. I'm just some kid who got tired of the bullshit in church. That's all. I'm not some great thinker ”. 
 
 “ Yes, that describes most of us. For every Leonardo there are a thousand people like you and me ”. 
 
 “ As in, da Vinci? I did n't know he was an atheist. ” 
 
 “ Eh, it's not about being an atheist, exactly. It's a long story, I'll explain later. Anyway Leonardo is one of our elders. He played a large role in the Uplifting War, when the Damned claimed ownership of Hell, threw out the angels, and built this city. Today he protects the outer wall ”. 
 
 “ From what? ” 
 
 “ Demons mostly. Sometimes an angelic scouting party. Do n't worry, the smart ones know not to fuck with Leo and his toys. For now, at least ”. 
 
 I sighed. My brain was still processing the glorious view out the window. Now that I had been staring at it for a while I was starting to notice details. The ground was covered in a red fog but I was able to make out something below it. They looked like criss-crossing lines. It seemed that there was no ground, only a fantastically massive grid upon which the city itself was built. The red light came from somewhere below. The glow waxed and waned, as if massive things moved beneath. 
 
 “ This is insane. I was alive yesterday, visiting my friend in Spokane. Now not only am I dead, I'm in Hell. And it's not what I expected. Shit, I did n't even think it was real ”. 
 
 “ Sorry, you have a lot to catch up on. And for what it's worth, I know exactly how you feel. I'm also new. Only been here since 1942. Anyway, you'll fit right in. And that brings me to my next point: It's time to start your training ”. 
 
 “ What training? ” 
 
 “ Long story short, tensions between Heaven and Hell are high. Ever since we pushed the angels out of Hell we've been running the show here. Hell is no longer a punishment, and the shiny folks upstairs are not happy about it. They're coming to put things back the way they were ”. 
 
 “ Who? Who's coming? ” 
 
 “ The Faithfull. The Reedemed. An army of Crusaders and Mujahideen led by angelic warriors. Word is Michael himself will be coordinating the attack ”. 
 
 “ Holy shit. What are we going to do against that? If they actually have God on their side what chance do we have? ” 
 
 A group of what appeared to be Apache helicopters crossed in front of the window before diving down into the red. 
 
 “ You have modern weapons? ” 
 
 “ Modern? ” she laughed. “ We have better than modern. This is what happens when the most brilliant minds in history gain access to the most powerful technology humanity ever came up with. We are n't just going to defend our city. We are going to break Heaven in half ”. 
 
 
 -- 
 
 
 Edit: I'm going to be continuing this over on /r/hfy under the title The Undamned. Right now only this first part is up there. The next chapter is coming in a couple days.

The city hums with life, a grid of many-colored buildings reaching towards the infinite void, housing the souls who chose to reject faith during their mortal existence. Yet, beneath us lies a fiery expanse, a constant reminder of the consequences of such choices.

His surprise is palpable, but quickly replaced with curiosity as he learns about our advanced city, our way of life, and the impending war against Heaven's forces led by Archangel Michael. And so, the war rages on above the fiery abyss, a battle between the fallen and the righteous. A battle that may decide the fate of both realms. From my post atop the city's wall, I stand as a silent witness to it all, an eternal guardian in this unconventional Hell.

name: ShieldsLastStand
source:
The undulating profiles of the warmth-hued pillars shook terribly as several muffled thuds, forming with a cacophony of distant screams and the ever-present roar of wailfire, echoed within the vast chamber. 
 
 In the center of the room, placing themselves in ranks five deep alongside the first pair of columns before the large brass doors - shaking more and more with each eternal minute. The Shields stood ready, plumed silver helmets gleaming in the sunset light poring into the room from the 
 crystal dome above. 
 
 Their armor, sleek and curved, powerful and steadfast, made each and every one of them resemble the tailed beasts that had forged the empire and that each and every one of them tamed for use. It too, gleamed in the setting light. 
 
 But each and every man had cuts, some deep, some shallow, somewhere on their body. They had bruises, they limped when they shifted their stance, their grips on their weapons sometimes slackened. They panted for breath, hoping that none of their comrades or their Lord-Commander would hear. But they refused to shirk from standing before the shaking door. 
 
 Behind them, Ranil squared his shoulders as the door began to shake with much more violence. He glanced at the men and women standing in a line in between the last pair of columns before the chuted flanges of the Penumbral Throne. `` What's moving out there?'' 
 
 One of them - a Guider - glanced over his shoulder at Ranis, moving his hands from his temples and taking a deep breath before coming over. `` The Archguard detects several hundred souls moving throughout the interior. A large portion of them are heading this way.'' 
 
 `` Right.'' Ranil gave the man a nod as he threw a look at the huge white throne behind him, catching a glimpse of a woman's tangled black hair and a pair of small grey eyes staring at him before shuffling out of sight. 
 
 He looked forward. `` Men! Lock shields and pull away from the doors!'' 
 
 Ranil's arm tensed as his fingers brushed against the hilt of the blade hanging from his hip. He took a moment to look behind him at the Throne again. 
 
 `` You probably wo n't get another chance, Ran.'' Ranil narrowed his eyes as he shook off the man's hand, turning to him. He stared at the thin man, dressed in a simple leather tunic with a pair of slitknives hanging from his chest and hips. He brushed his wild hair from his eyes. `` There wo n't be much time.'' 
 
 Ranil's eyes softened as he nodded. Silently he turned away, walking towards the throne. He stopped at the base of the steps leading to the throne itself for a moment before shaking his head and moving past it, skirting the steps until he came to the shadowy high backed slab the Penumbral Throne leapt from like a physical shadow. 
 
 A boy sat crouched, his knees tucked up and his back against the harsh black stone as he turned over the gleaming white band of metal in his hands. 
 
 The boy's shoulders gently shook as tears streamed down his cheeks, his little breaths shuddering in fright each time a massive boom echoed throughout the chamber. 
 
 Ranil knelt next to him, reaching a rough hand to cup the boy's cheek. `` Hush, little one.'' 
 
 The boy's sobs continued as he dropped the circlet to the polished marble floor with a echoing clatter and wrapped his arms around the man's sides, pressing his face into his chest. `` I'm scared - they're coming and-'' 
 
 Ranil gave a gentle smile as he placed his hand on the boy's head, ruffling his black hair. `` You must remain strong. For you and her.'' He jerked his chin at the woman, cradling a baby in her arms. 
 
 The doors pounded, and the massive hinges squealed in protest. The Shields tensed up, readying their spears. 
 
 Near the columns one of the Guiders cried out and fell to the floor, clutching at his head as his eyes started to bleed as hoarse strangled words of a strange tongue tumbled out amid his dying breaths. 
 
 `` Ran! Time's up! The shimmerwall is about to fail!'' The wild-haired man yelled, striding over as the Guiders dragged away their dead comrade and closed ranks again, grabbing each other's hands as the gems embedded in their palms began to shine with burning light. 
 
 The boy's breaths began to quicken as his hands started to shake. He stared up at Ranil, tears brimming. Ranil continued to hold him close, before pulling away and hoisting the boy to his feet, picking up the circlet and placing it in his hands. 
 
 `` I failed your mother. I will not fail you.'' 
 
 He looked over at the woman as she came over, clutching the baby in her arms. `` Ranil-'' 
 
 `` You need to get him out of here, Isha. Hide yourselves away.'' 
 
 `` But-'' 
 
 `` I need to stay. You need to go.'' 
 
 `` Ranis-'' 
 
 `` I wo n't forget you. And I'll be damned if you forget me.'' Ranil pulled her into a quick embrace, giving her a gentle peck on the head before. 
 
 `` Never, big brother.'' Isha whispered, grinding her teeth as she fought against the tears welling in her eyes, shifting her grip on the baby as she grabbed the boy's hand. 
 
 Ranil turned sidelong, narrowing his eyes as the doors continued to shake with more and more violence as several pure white cracks began to widen in the sheer brass surface. He exhaled as he drew the slender sword at his hip, keeping his grip light but firm. `` I will see you in the next world.'' 
 
 As he said this white cracks began to snake out across the huge doors, joining together as a ear-splitting screech began to fill the room, forcing some of the Shields to their knees and downing a few Guiders. 
 
 `` The shimmerwall!'' 
 
 The doors blasted inward with a explosive flash, metal screaming, men shouting, a huge spindly black beast screeching in triumph as its bladed claws sank into the pulverized brass slabs hanging off their hinges, ripping them free and tossing them through the air. 
 
 The Shields moved backwards as one force, avoiding the slabs as dark shapes began to appear in the dust surrounding the throne room entry. 
 
 Ranil beckoned to the wild-haired man. `` Malir! Take them away from here! Use your slipways!'' 
 
 The smuggler nodded, jogging over to Isha and guiding her, the baby and the boy to a small door hidden in the shadowy corners behind the Penumbral Throne. `` Consider my debt done!'' 
 
 Ranil smirked. `` Definitely, old friend.'' 
 
 The boy struggled and tugged against Isha and Malir, grunting and screaming the entire way before the four of them disappeared through the little door. 
 
 Ranil made sure they were gone before glancing at a nearby mage. `` Seal it behind them!'' 
 
 The young woman nodded, pointing at the door. The wood splintered and cracked, crumpling inwards and leaving behind only a twisted wooden hulk. 
 
 The Shields shouted as one as a dark figure deftly moved through the doorway amidst the screeches of the black beast, his icy eyes landing on Ranil in a instant. 
 
 `` Lord-Commander. You've failed in your duties.''
retelling:
Narrated by Malir, the unnamed smuggler:

In the shadowy corners of a grand chamber, where warm-hued pillars stood like ancient guardians, I found myself huddled amidst a sea of heavily armed soldiers, the Shields. Their faces were etched with fatigue and fear as they stood rigid before massive brass doors that trembled ominously. The air was thick with the cacophony of screams and a roaring "wailfire," echoing off the crystal dome ceiling high above us.

A Guider, a figure of authority in this place, approached Ranil - a leader amongst the soldiers. He informed Ranil that several hundred entities were approaching, casting a sense of unease among the Shields. I watched as Ranil, his eyes hard and determined, delegated the safety of a young boy and a woman with a baby, the boy’s mother and sister, to me.

I accepted the responsibility, my heart pounding in my chest. I knew that the magical barrier, the "shimmerwall," was beginning to falter, its once impenetrable glow dimming. As the doors broke open, unleashing monstrous creatures, Ranil ensured the safe passage of the boy, his mother, and sister via a hidden escape route concealed behind the Penumbral Throne.

I followed close behind them, my thoughts racing with worry for Ranil as he faced the incoming threat alone. I couldn't help but feel a sense of admiration for his selfless act, knowing full well that he was sacrificing himself to save others. A dark figure emerged from the chaos, addressing him with a declaration of failure.

But it wasn't failure I saw in Ranil's eyes as he stood defiant against the tide of evil. It was bravery, honor, and an unwavering commitment to protecting those he loved. In that moment, I understood why this place and its people were worth fighting for - because heroes like Ranil existed within their midst.

name: LateMacAndCheeseDate
source:
I was standing just outside the doors to reception feeling rather upset with myself. I was fifteen minutes late with no feasible explanation. I have one best friend that does n't live in the same city, no boyfriend, my family is passive about my existence and my coworkers only notice me when they need something. 
 
 There was n't a whole lot to distract me and I was looking forward to homemade macaroni and cheese for lunch. I had bought all the ingredients last night and had no reason to deviate from my plans. 
 
 Finally I only had ten minutes left. Feeling anxious I thought maybe something awful had happened. I was hungry, though, and as I lightly jogged to the corner coffee shop to grab a tea and muffin, I hoped I had n't died. By the time I got back into work I thought maybe the time machine had malfunctioned. 
 
 By the end of the day there was no sign of me to indicate that the machine had been fixed. I packed up my things and made to leave. On the way out one of the new hires bumped into me and knocked my phone out of my hand as I was plugging my headphones into it. 
 
 He picked it up and said, `` Funny how we do n't even have music players anymore. Everyone just uses their phone.'' 
 
 He was smiling at me and he was awfully attractive. I was too distracted by the thought that he may be flirting to properly reply. He cleared his throat and introduced himself, `` I'm Dennis.'' 
 
 I blinked, `` Uh, hi. I'm Karen.'' 
 
 We started to the elevator together. He talked about his old job on the way down to the main floor and I just listened. He asked me about how long I'd worked there and held the front door open for me. I was about to thank him for being such a gentleman when he suddenly asked me if I wanted to go get dinner somewhere. 
 
 `` Like a date?'' The words came out faster than my brain thought them. I had n't been on a date in nearly a year. I almost covered my face up when he laughed and said, `` Yeah, I guess. I do n't know, you're cute so far.'' 
 
 So we got on the bus together and went the opposite way of home. He lived closer to downtown while I lived out the outskirts, in the suburbs. His commute was a fraction of mine but it would make my trip home much longer anyway. It did n't matter much to me though, as each time he smile at me my stomach seemed to acquire additional butterflies. 
 
 He suggested a local bar that I had n't ever been to. Dennis did a fair job of making me laugh on the way there. He had a geeky sense of humor that I appreciated even though I did n't get most of the references he made. 
 
 When we got to the bar and looked at the menu I was so happy to see that they had mac'n'cheese. It was even pictured and did n't appear to be the cheap, microwaved kind. Of course I ordered it and to my delight the serving was huge - there was leftovers to take home. 
 
 Dennis invited me back to his place for what he called'cheaper drinks', insisting we go because he claimed it was still early and besides, he lived'literally two blocks away'. Two blocks ended up being four. 
 
 We did have those drinks. Maybe it was the alcohol or that I had been involuntarily abstinent for quite a while, but for the first time ever I slept with someone on a first date. 
 
 Before I left for home we made plans to see each other again. He teased me and called me on the number he had made me put in his phone to confirm that it was mine. I kissed him goodbye and got on the bus home smiling. 
 
 That smile dropped when I realized I left my leftovers on his kitchen counter. 
 
 I debated whether or not I should go tell myself why I would n't be getting macaroni and cheese earlier that day, but I've decided not to. Now that I'm home and feeling the way that I do, even though I'm still a bit disappointed that I forgot my leftovers, I think that some surprises should be left to be surprises.
retelling:

   As a fresh face in the bustling corporate world, I, Dennis, found myself navigating the labyrinthine corridors of my new workplace on my first day. name: SanctuaryCatWar
source:
I was walking home from work in the cold sleet, wishing I had a car. No one did, not anymore. All the vehicles not used by the military were scrapped for the war. I lived in The Sanctuary, one of the few human cities independent of the Animal Kingdoms. We had to fight every day to maintain it, and military service was mandatory. I had worked at an ammunition factory for 3 years, ever since I was 14. After 4 years of civil service I'd only have to serve one year instead of two. I took this program because the pay's decent, and the average soldier lives for a few months. 
 
 Pets are nonexsitant here, but there are `` stray'' cats and dogs all over the place. On civil service program involves rounding all these up, but many evade them. These `` strays'', as all school children know, are very aggressive and hostile to humans, often growling and barking before scampering off; however, cats have never been like that to me. My friends would be hissed at and scratched, but I could pick them up and they'd purr with delight. This was noticed by many people, including the Ministry of Defence who feared that I, like the `` stray'' animals, was a spy. 
 
 Walking down the deserted alleyway, I heard a low rumble from behind. I turned, only to be confronted with two leopards. I tried to run, but a third leopard blocked my escape. They lunged, and slashed me across the chest. One tackled me, but was pulled away by a massive german shepherd. A pack of the biggest dogs I've ever seen flooded the alleyway, and parlayed with the big cats. I ran, and was stopped by a pitbull. It wanted me to follow it, and I did. It lead me out of the city. Along the way, I'd see small flocks of birds badger random areas on rooftops, only for a tomcat or two to spill out and get chased off. A few were scooped up by hawks. 
 
 Crawling through a small tunnel that smelled awful, I emerged in a forest, and collapsed from the shock and massive lesions across my chest. I awoke in a room. I could see the walls of Sanctuary out my window. I heard a knock at my door and two middle aged men came in. They introduced themselves as the King of Dogs and the Lord of Birds. I was in a fortress and main base of operations for the two men's war against the Queen of Cats. They told me I shared here affinity with cats, and that she wanted to kill me and take out a possible rival. My powers are weak now and I can barely control cats, but eventually they'll develop enough to rival her's. I was rescued so that they may use me as a weapon, I could undermine her powers and give them the edge they need to win. 
 
 I've been kept here for 40 days now. While I'm free to walk around the castle I'm escorted by sheep dogs and birds watch my every move. Lately I've been confined to my room. I have a marvelous view of the dogs and birds heading to the front. Everyday a column of dogs marches off in eager spirits. Every night, an equally large column of wounded dogs limps back. My room is right above the infirmary, the howls of anguish and the yelps of the doomed keep me awake for hours. The columns marching off have been getting smaller, and the ones marching back are getting larger. I see fewer and fewer birds flitting about. The war goes poorly. The dogs and birds have been fighting amongst eachother. The amiable sheep dog was replaced by a pack of mean wolves and a cassowary. 
 
 Tonight, I was awoken by a soft voice repeating `` Wake up, wake up.'' I opened my eyes to see a cat standing on my chest. I jumped up but was hushed. `` Silence in golden right now.'' the cat began `` The Queen apologizes for the excessive forced used earlier, it really was over the top but you were incapable of understanding us at the time. The Queen wishes to have you in her palace. She is an old woman, and here years are numbered. While twice as powerful as her adversaries, thanks to her age, she is almost 80, and needs an heir. Come with me, we can smuggle you out and take you to the palace.'' 
 
 `` I'm not sure I trust you.'' I proclaimed. 
 
 `` That's understandible, but we're your best bet for survival. The dogs and birds have lost, their line has collapsed, the cheetahs have the area surrounded. There is a rift in the alliance. The Lord of Birds is retreating, and wishes to take you away with him. He's really bad at keeping a secret, since everyone knows and the King of Dogs wants to kill you. You ca n't return to Sanctuary either, as you were declared an enemy of the species and had your humanity formally revoked. If you could make it to their trenches alive you'll be shot on sight. Hurry now, with me. If you run away with the birds and are inevitably captured when the birds get intercepted no mercy shall be shown to you.'' 
 
 So now here I am. The cassowary was killed outside by the sound of it. I can see the King of Dogs marching through the courtyard with a group of wolves. I can here dogs and birds fighting out in the hallway. My only choice appears to be with the Queen of Cats, and I do n't by that `` excessive force'' story. I fear this may be the end for me.
retelling:
Character: The Cat (unnamed)

   In the heart of the Animal Kingdoms, a world teeming with conflict and intrigue, I, an ordinary cat, found myself on a mission that would forever change the course of my life. The city of humans, known as Sanctuary, was under siege, its walls echoing with the constant clash of arms and steel. As a loyal subject of the Queen of Cats, I had sworn to uphold her rule, but events were unfolding that threatened to disrupt the delicate balance of power between our kingdoms.

   The King of Dogs and the Lord of Birds had united their forces, seeking to overthrow the ruling monarch. Their armies stretched as far as the eye could see, encircling the fortress that served as our stronghold. It was a grim sight, with the scent of blood and smoke hanging heavy in the air.

   One day, a human entered our midst. He was unlike any other I had ever seen, his eyes filled with fear yet tinged with an unspoken courage. The other cats regarded him with suspicion, their fur bristling at his presence. He belonged to them but not of us - a spy, they said. Yet, there was something about him that intrigued me.

   I watched as the leopards attacked the human, their fangs bared in a brutal display of power. The other cats fled, leaving him vulnerable. But not I. In a moment of instinctual bravery, I intervened, driving the leopards away and saving his life. He was weakened by his wounds, but I could sense that he was no ordinary human.

   We brought the wounded stranger to our fortress, where the King of Dogs and the Lord of Birds plotted their next move. The human's affinity for cats intrigued them, making him a valuable asset in their war against the Queen of Cats. They held him captive, using his unique abilities as a weapon against her.

   As the tide of battle began to turn against the King and the Lord, a desperate plea came from the Queen's palace. She sought an heir and believed that this human could provide it. A cat emissary was sent to negotiate with him, offering him sanctuary in her palace if he chose to join her cause.

   And so, I found myself standing at a crossroads, my fate intertwined with that of the human. He faced a life-or-death choice, torn between allegiance to his own kind and the potential future of our kingdoms. I watched as he wrestled with his decision, his eyes filled with the weight of responsibility.

   And in that moment, I realized that I had become more than just an observer. I had become a part of their story, a silent witness to the unfolding drama of this world. I vowed to protect him, to stand by his side, no matter the consequences. For it was not just our future at stake but the very balance of power in the Animal Kingdoms.

name: GraveyardWoolCaper
source:
His mother's funeral was terrible for Jake, but coming back the next day to find a piece of black wool tied around her gravestone sparked intrigue rather than anger. The piece of wool seemed to be still connected to something. He followed the piece of wool through the graveyard and ended up right at the door of a mausoleum. He tentatively walked inside, afraid to disturb the living, when he was suddenly attacked from behind. Luckily for him, his assailant was an odd, odd man and had tried to bash him head in with an old, rusted trumpet which did nothing but give him a little bit of tetanus. Jake recovered quickly, and punched the man in the face. 
 
 As the man stumbled outside the mausoleum and into the sunlight, Jake noticed that he had on a monocle and a top hat. More confused and more intrigued than he was earlier, he went out to confront the man. But before he could get a word out, the man hopped out of sight. Jake searched for the man, but could n't find him. He turned to go back into the mausoleum. Hearing something behind him, Jake turned around to see that the man was rushing at him on a pennyfarthing at a surprisingly high speed. Quickly reacting, Jake jumped out of the way and grabbed the black wool. As the front wheel of the pennyfarthing crossed over, Jake pulled the piece of wool taut, causing it to catch the back wheel, sending the man flying off of his pennyfarthing and into the mausoleum. 
 
 Jake walked into the mausoleum to find that the man had broken through a thin plaster wall and had fallen down the stairs. He followed the stairs down until he reached the dying body of the strange man. Jake bent down to talk to him. 
 
 `` You know, even if you did manage to hit me, you still would have gone flying down here like you did. There's a reason people use cars for hit and runs, and not pennyfarthings.'' 
 
 The man cough more blood out of his mouth and beckoned Jake closer with his finger. Jake brought his ear to the mans mouth. The man died as he said his last words. 
 
 `` You're right. Fucknuggets.'' 
 
 Jake was confused, but banked the word for later usage. He continued walking down the stairs for around three minutes, all the while thinking how much more irritating it would be to have to walk back up. At the bottom of the staircase was a room with a big door on the other end of it. In front of the door were two deep half circles cut into the stone in front of it. Next to the two indents was a refrigerator. A curious Jake opened the refrigerator, and inside found two dozen eggs and a pamphlet. Opening up the pamphlet, Jake found the instructions to get the door open. He had to separate the eggs and fill up both holes, one with egg whites, and the other with the yolks. He started to crack and separate eggs. 
 
 By the time he filled up a third of the yolk hole, the egg white hole was filled. 
 
 `` Damnit,'' he cursed. What am I gon na do with the rest of the egg white?'' 
 
 It was then he heard the sound of two objects sliding, one a stone, and another metal object. He turned to face the refrigerator, and realized that there was a nice electric stove now next to it. On top of the stove was a nice, large pan. Jake turned on the stove to heat up the pan. He then separated the eggs, putting the yolks in the ground and the white in the pan. When he finished, he had an egg white omelet that could keep his family for a week. It was at this moment that Jake remember that he had no family, because his mom was dead. The door slid open, and a couple of stacked, decaying bodies fell from the open door, landing face first in the yolk. Jake walked over the bodies and into the newly opened room, only to find the last set of instructions for Fucknugget Cupcakes. He rolled his eyes and left, wondering why he thought he would find something more than a couple dead bodies and a strange cupcake recipe in the mausoleum, which was, after all, still a mausoleum. 
 
 He wandered back to his mother's grave, only to the find the gravestone lying down on the floor, having been pulled out by the man on the pennyfarthing. Jake sat down and tried to put the gravestone back, but it kept falling back down. Jake grabbed a length of the wool and sat down on a bench nearby, keeping his mother's gravestone slightly angled, but upright. Jake sat still, holding up his mother's gravestone before the police came and arrested him for voluntary manslaughter. The gravestone made a solid sound as it fell back down.
retelling:
Narrative Perspective: The Odd Man/Assailant (Referred to as "Fucknugget" posthumously)

In the grand expanse of an eerie graveyard, I, Fucknugget, found myself drawn towards a particular gravesite - that of Jake's Mother. The pull was inexplicable yet undeniable, my heart racing as I crept closer under the veil of the moonlight. My top hat and monocle, a stark contrast against the darkness, seemed to taunt me with their sinister allure.

I had come prepared for this meeting, armed with an unusual weapon - a rusty trumpet that held a mysterious charm. I knew the graveyard well enough to avoid detection as I made my way towards the gravesite, ready to claim what was mine.

As I reached the grave, my eyes fell upon a piece of black wool attached to it. A curious detail, one that piqued my interest. Intrigued, I followed the thread into the depths of the mausoleum, feeling a strange sense of anticipation wash over me.

Once inside, I was confronted by Jake - a young man whose resolve I underestimated. Our encounter was brief but intense, fueled by the tension that filled the air. I retreated, vowing to return stronger and more prepared for our next meeting.

True to my word, I returned on a penny-farthing bicycle, an ironic choice considering the somber setting. This time, I was determined to claim what I had come for - the black wool that seemed to beckon me from the gravesite.

Our second confrontation was more heated than our first. In a fit of rage and frustration, I lost control, and with one wrong move, I found myself tumbling into the mausoleum's depths. The fall was painful, but it was the sound of my own bones snapping that silenced me forever.

In the aftermath, Jake discovered a hidden room containing a refrigerator with eggs and a pamphlet detailing a puzzle to open a door. He solved the puzzle imperfectly, revealing more decaying bodies and a recipe for "Fucknugget Cupcakes." Ironic, isn't it?

In the end, Jake sat by his mother's grave, the police arriving to arrest him for manslaughter. But little did they know, it was my own recklessness that had led to my demise. The story of our confrontation would live on, a strange tale of mystery and intrigue in the heart of a graveyard.

 `` That's it?''

 `` Immune to reality warping?''

name: MorningPremonition
source:
My wife was sleeping peacefully next to me. I smoothed a curl that clung to her neck and kissed her on the cheek. Lazily, she woke and smiled. 
 
 We moved for a while, kissing and generally enjoying ourselves. Eventually she sat up. She was beautiful like this. Hair wild, eyes bright. Naked in bed. 
 
 I scanned her form slowly, enjoying her curves and the look on her face as she watched me. Her slender neck, sloping shoulders, perfect breasts, glowing stomach.... Wait what? 
 
 My heart sank. I strained my eyes, trying to convince myself that what I saw was just a trick of the light. 
 
 There was no mistake. 
 
 My wife was pregnant, and the child inside her would one day be my undoing. My family gift, knowing what person or thing would kill us, has never been more of a curse. 
 
 `` Honey?'' My wife's concerned voice breaks through my thoughts. I force a smile on my face. 
 
 `` Yes dear?''

retelling:
Perspective: The Unborn Child (Referred to as "Little One")

In the quiet recesses of darkness, I drifted, suspended in a warm embrace. The soft hums and gentle murmurs surrounding me were familiar – they belonged to my parents. It was nighttime, the time when our family reunited, nestled within the confines of a cozy bed in a place called home.

One day, I sensed a subtle shift. My mother's heartbeat quickened, and her breath grew shallower. I was aware of the change, even though I couldn't yet comprehend its implications.

The following morning, something extraordinary happened. As my father opened his eyes to greet the new day, he felt a strange sensation – a mix of joy and unease stirring within him. He lay there, gazing at my mother, his dear wife, who continued to sleep peacefully beside him.

In that moment, the knowledge that had lain dormant within my father was awakened. It was the family gift he carried – the premonition of his own demise. But as he looked upon my sleeping mother, it became apparent that this premonition would not be solely his burden anymore.

As the days passed, I continued to grow stronger within my mother's womb. And with each passing day, my father's worry and discomfort grew. He didn't understand why he felt this way – after all, I was a part of him, a part of our family. But the gift he carried warned him that one day, his presence would be required elsewhere, leaving us behind.

I couldn't help but wonder what it was like on the other side, where my father resided before entering this cozy sanctuary. I heard stories of laughter, love, and adventure – things I longed to experience firsthand. But now that I knew of his impending departure, a sense of urgency filled me. I yearned to connect with him, to learn from him, to be with him one last time before he left us forever.

And so, as the days turned into weeks and weeks into months, my father began to find solace in our shared moments. He would speak to me softly, telling stories of his life, sharing words of wisdom, and whispering sweet nothings that I held close to my heart.

On the day my mother delivered me into the world, my father was by her side, a mix of joy and sadness etched upon his face. He looked at me, this tiny being who would one day carry on our family line, and knew that his time with us was drawing near.

The days following my birth were filled with love and laughter. But I could sense the underlying tension – a weight my father carried like a cloak. I couldn't understand it then, but as I grew older and came to learn more about our family gift, I would come to see that it was the knowledge of his own demise that hung over us all, like a heavy cloud in the sky.

As for me, I held on to every moment with my father, cherishing each memory and soaking up every word he spoke. I knew that one day, he would be called away, leaving us behind. But until then, we were a family – bound by love, fate, and our shared gift. And as I grew older, I would come to learn that the weight my father carried was not a burden but a testament to the strength of our bond.

name: CellarSearch
source:
The noises above the cellar announced the search had begun. Ayl put a finger on his lips and looked at each member of his family. Joba nodded, little Ki clutched to her chest. Minu and Tau also nodded vigorously, putting dutiful fingers on their lips. The searched edged closer. Minu closed her eyes, hands joined in prayer. Tau curled up on the floor. Joba looked up at the trapdoor. Ayl looked around for some means of protection, or defense. 
 
 Shouts from above. Orders barked. 
 
 Ki stirred and began to make a sound, Joba's mouth quickly closed over her baby's mouth, even as she rocked the tiny body, whispering sweetly. The baby would not quiet, it's muffled sounds felt like a cacophony. 
 
 Louder noises from above. They would be caught. Ayl had to act. He looked wildly in his wife's eyes. She looked serene, understanding. 
 
 -- -- -- 
 
 Four of them survived the search. The family was forever broken.
retelling:
Perspective: Ki, the baby

In the dim and narrow confines of a cellar, I find myself surrounded by familiar faces – Ayl, Joba, Minu, Tau, and my mother. It's a small space, cozy yet cramped, and it echoes with strange noises from outside. These sounds are loud and frightening, like the patter of heavy feet or the rustle of many moving parts.

I don't understand what's happening above us, but I can sense my family's tension. Their faces are serious, their eyes wide with fear. They hush me when I cry, pressing soft cloths against my cheeks and murmuring soothing words.

The silence is broken only by the distant noises above, and I startle easily at every sound. Each creak or thud causes a ripple of worry among my family members, their eyes darting around the cellar as they listen intently.

I can't help but cry again, unable to comprehend why they're so scared. But Ayl takes me in her arms and whispers soft lullabies, rocking me gently back and forth. Despite my mother's efforts, I sense that something terrible is coming for us.

In the end, I can hear the sounds of struggle, followed by cries of pain. My family huddles together, their faces twisted in agony as they shield one another. When it all goes quiet once more, I know something has changed – our family will never be whole again. But even in my innocence, I understand that we must persevere and remain strong for each other.

The cellar, once a sanctuary, now feels like a prison. The darkness presses in on me as I drift off to sleep, held tightly by Ayl, knowing that tomorrow will bring new challenges – but I trust that my family will face them together.

name: RainyDayClicks
source:
It was raining again. Not that there was anything wrong with that, it was just an unfortunate day to take some pictures. But then again Sam never knew what to capture once he could actually walk through the gardens, parks and streets. 
 
 *click* 
 
 With the rain keeping him inside the house he had no choice but to watch TV or play a game on his PC. Sure he could take pictures of the rain but with only one camera he would n't risk it getting wet. So off to the living room he went. His father was there drinking his fifth cup of coffee while his mother slowly browsed through the channels. 
 
 *click* 
 
 Even with the ability to record several hundred hours of TV and a connection to the internet, it always felt like there was nothing to watch. Sam had learned not to disturb the parental routine of watching and flipping mindlessly, somehow it made things feel like home. 
 
 *click* 
 
 Getting to the PC would be easy, he just hoped that he could play at least one level before his Brother had to use the thing for something. It was always like that. No one needs the PC until Sam wants to play a game and with the rain settling in the chances are that he wo n't be left alone for long. 
 
 *click* 
 Do it slower... 
 *click* 
 *click* 
 FFS! 
 
 Nothing could take the joy of shooting another Russian in the face. Always taking up too much space on the servers. Sam was having fun playing BF4 and his friends had just logged in when he felt a tap on his shoulder. His brother was there, ready to chase him away and tell him he needed the PC for `` work''. Because looking at weird pictures and browsing the internet meant work. 
 
 *Click* 
 
 With the TV taken and PC being underused there was only one thing left that Sam could do. Lying in bed and reading a book. Sam had been reading mysteries lately and they had actually caused him to be a bit more paranoid in his everyday life. Just a few days before at College what Sam thought was a grand mystery, why the blonde girl that sits next to him had disappeared, was actually just a simple case of her getting tired of his weird hand movements. 
 
 *Click* 
 *Click* 
 stop it! 
 *Click* 
 *Click* 
 
 It was March again and Sam had Broken up with Alice, she was sweet but also amazingly negative... 
 
 *Click* 
 Dammit now we skipped several months, you know I ca n't read that fast. Stop skipping pages just because you find you're getting bored. We're all stuck in here with only the one Kindle. If you do n't stop I will slap some sense into you, you know once I can find the particles that my arms used to be. 
 
 Ziandar was n't enjoying being stuck in a black hole with his henchman. Somehow they had control of the Kindle and he was the only one that could see the screen. They just liked pressing the buttons. It looked like eternity was going to be a very, very long time...
retelling:
Narrated by Ziandar's Henchman:

In the depths of a churning abyss, I found myself ensnared in an unfathomable black hole, alongside my master, Ziandar. The void was a silent and menacing presence, swallowing all light and sound, save for the occasional echo of our own breaths. We were no longer mere prisoners; we had become spectral entities manipulating the fabric of reality itself.

One day, our reach extended beyond the confines of this cosmic prison, seeping into a distant world - Earth. Our target: a Kindle, owned by an insignificant creature named Sam. Unbeknownst to us, this device would become the conduit through which we could torment and amuse ourselves for eons to come.

As Sam sat in his cozy bedroom, engrossed in his mystery novel, our control over his Kindle began to take effect. The pages turned with a satisfying click, interrupting Sam's escape into the story. His frustration was palpable as he struggled to regain control of his device and immerse himself once more in the world of fiction.

Meanwhile, on the other side of the universe, Ziandar reveled in our newfound power. I could feel his excitement pulsating through the dark matter that bound us together. He commanded me to increase the frequency of our interruptions and to delve further into Sam's life, feeding off his emotions and using them to fuel our own existence.

As days turned into weeks, we grew bolder and more daring. We learned about Sam's past - the heartbreak he experienced with a girl named Alice and the challenges he faced at college. We laughed as he grew increasingly frantic in his attempts to shake off our influence and reclaim control of his life.

In the end, we were content to remain trapped in the black hole, feeding on Sam's life for all eternity. The dance between us was a never-ending symphony, a cosmic ballet of power and torment. And as I drifted off into the void, I knew that our story would continue for all time, an eternal reminder of the power of manipulation and control.
